title: Staff Data Engineer
description:
RevolutionParts is not just a pioneering force in the automotive eCommerce realm; we're actively seeking passionate and talented individuals to join our squad of Revolutionaries (yes, that's what we call ourselves!). As leaders in providing streamlined, user-friendly solutions, we empower automotive brands to maximize online sales. Our commitment to technology, top-notch customer service, and a profound understanding of the automotive market sets us apart. If you're ready to revolutionize the eCommerce space for automotive parts and accessories, consider joining our dynamic team of Revolutionaries.

The Role
Most data engineering roles hand you a Jira board. This one hands you a whiteboard and asks what should be on it.
RevolutionParts powers parts and accessories commerce for thousands of automotive dealers and OEMs across North America. The data behind all of it (catalog, pricing, inventory) moves through a high-volume ingestion system that has scaled with the business. It was the right architecture for where we were. It isn’t the right architecture for where we’re going.

We need someone who can keep this system reliable today while making it obsolete on a timeline they define.
The target architecture doesn't exist yet. The technical bar for this domain gets set by whoever takes this role. If that's an uncomfortable amount of open space, this probably isn't the right fit. If it sounds like the kind of problem worth leaving your current job for, read on.

Responsibilities


Strategic Leadership & Architectural Ownership
  • You are the technical authority for data ingestion at RevolutionParts. You lead through expertise, not authority.
  • Own the 2-3 year architectural vision for data ingestion. That means the destination, the migration sequence, the tradeoffs at each stage, and the criteria that determine when the current system has earned its retirement.
  • Set the engineering standards that govern how every team builds on and interfaces with core data infrastructure: schema design, data contracts, query optimization, observability. What you establish here becomes the organization’s baseline.
  • Shape technical strategy across Product, BI, Platform Engineering, and Executive Leadership. Not as an advisor. As the person who drives alignment, cuts through ambiguity, and owns the outcomes of complex multi-quarter initiatives from discovery through delivery.
  • Take ownership of the highest-severity, most ambiguous problems in the data domain: the ones that cross team boundaries, have no clear owner, and have already resisted resolution.

Execution & Operational Excellence

  • Hold ultimate accountability for the architecture and production performance of our catalog, pricing, and inventory ingestion systems, with the technical depth to make decisions no one else in the organization is positioned to make.
  • Define the reliability bar for data across the organization. Build the monitoring, alerting, and validation frameworks that turn data quality from a best-effort into a contractual commitment with clear SLAs and owners.
  • Make final, binding technical debt decisions for the ingestion domain, weighing immediate stability against long-term architectural health. Document the reasoning with enough clarity that it survives organizational change 18 months from now.
  • Elevate the technical ceiling of the data engineering organization through direct mentorship of Senior Engineers on distributed systems, high-volume database performance, and data modeling at scale. Your impact here compounds beyond your own output.

Requirements


10+ years in data or software engineering, at least 3 at Staff level or equivalent owning architectural decisions on high-volume production systems.

Python and Spark/PySpark at petabyte scale — production systems, not notebooks. You tune Spark from first principles: partition strategy, join optimization, dynamic allocation, skew diagnosis.
  • Designed and operated distributed job execution systems: dynamic compute provisioning, variable workload profiles, job isolation, and resource contention at scale.
  • Deep experience with message queue architectures in production: fan-out patterns, poison pill handling, dead letter queues, consumer lag at scale.
  • Built observability into systems that had none — monitoring, alerting, lineage, and pipeline health designed in from the ground up, not dashboards bolted on afterward.

Built pipeline orchestration infrastructure, not just DAGs. You have strong opinions about operability because you've inherited systems that weren't.

  • You set the engineering quality bar. Reliable, efficient, documented, testable, maintainable — and you hold the team to the same standard.

Led a migration from legacy batch infrastructure (custom schedulers, daemon-based systems, cron pipelines) to modern architecture without taking down production. We'll go deep on this in the interview.
  • Deep AWS in production: EKS, EC2 fleet management, SQS, RDS. Operated at scale, not just deployed into it.
  • Kubernetes in production — workload behavior, compute right-sizing for variable job profiles, failure modes under load.
  • Streaming in production: Kafka, Flink, Kinesis, or Redpanda. You've made the batch-vs-streaming call in both directions and can defend either.
  • Cloud data warehouse architecture — Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks. Clustering, partitioning, cost management, mixed analytical and operational workloads.
  • You use AI coding tools daily and have shipped production work because of it.
  • You write architecture docs engineers trust and can brief a VP on the same decision. Both matter at this level.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent.

AI Fluency & Modern Tooling
At RevolutionParts, we expect team members to actively use modern tools — including AI-powered systems — to improve decision-making, productivity, and quality of work.
This includes:
  • Using AI tools responsibly to accelerate research, analysis, documentation, and problem-solving
  • Exercising strong judgment around data privacy, accuracy, and ethical use
  • Continuously learning and adapting as AI capabilities evolve
Proven examples of using AI to improve outcomes in prior roles is expected.

RevolutionParts is proud to provide all full-time Revolutionaries with a comprehensive employment package including competitive compensation, career development, benefits, 401K match, parental leave, and many more valuable perks. You can learn more about our core-value driven culture at our career page.

RevolutionParts is an Equal Opportunity Employer; we value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender orientation, gender identity or expression, sexual identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family status, genetic information, veteran status, or disability status.

Please Note: You will only receive correspondence through the GEM ATS or from a @revolutionparts.com email address. If you are receiving communication through any other platform or domain, it may be fraudulent, and we urge you to ignore the communication.

title: Staff / Principal Battery Systems Engineer – Performance & Integration
location: Fremont, California; Irvine, California; Manteno, Illinois
description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

About the Role

Gotion is strengthening its North American EV engineering organization to support next-generation battery programs with leading automotive customers.

We are looking for an experienced Staff / Principal Battery Systems Engineer – Performance & Integration to serve as a key technical owner for HV battery system performance and integration in North America.

This is not a component-level design or test-only role. You will work at the intersection of vehicle requirements, battery cells, pack systems, BMS/controls, thermal systems, and validation, translating customer vehicle-level requirements into battery system targets and driving technical decisions through development, validation, and vehicle integration.

The role will have significant visibility with both customers and Gotion’s global engineering teams and offers the opportunity to help shape our North American battery systems engineering capability.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and drive HV battery system performance and integration for North American EV programs, from customer requirements through system validation and issue resolution.
  • Translate vehicle-level requirements into system, pack, cell, BMS, thermal, and validation requirements and performance targets.
  • Lead technical trade-off analysis across energy, power, fast charging, thermal performance, durability, aging, safety, cost, and packaging.
  • Serve as a primary technical interface between OEM customers and Gotion’s Cell, Pack, BMS, Thermal, Electrical, CAE, and Validation teams.
  • Develop and maintain system-level requirements, performance specifications, SORs, DFMEAs, diagnostic requirements, and technical documentation.
  • Analyze battery and vehicle data to identify performance limitations and root causes and drive cross-functional resolution.
  • Support and technically lead battery performance validation, including fast charging, cold/hot weather, power capability, energy/range, aging, and vehicle-level testing.
  • Partner with BMS and controls teams on SOC/SOH, power limits, charging strategy, fault handling, diagnostics, and system-level control requirements.
  • Support vehicle launch and field issue resolution, ensuring technical issues are driven to closure across customer and internal engineering organizations.
  • Help establish system engineering methodologies, technical standards, and engineering capability for Gotion’s growing North American EV organization.
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineers and influence technical decisions across programs without relying solely on organizational authority.

What We’re Looking For

  • BS/MS/PhD in Electrical, Mechanical, Chemical, Automotive, Systems Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 7+ years of experience in EV, HV battery, battery pack, or electrified powertrain systems engineering. Exceptional candidates with fewer years but significant system ownership experience will be considered.
  • Strong understanding of HV battery system architecture, including cells, modules, packs, BMS, HV components, thermal systems, sensing, charging, and vehicle interfaces.
  • Demonstrated experience in at least several of the following:
    • Battery system architecture and requirements
    • Battery performance and characterization
    • Vehicle / battery systems integration
    • BMS and controls interface
    • Fast charging and power capability
    • SOC / SOH / aging
    • Thermal performance
    • System validation and vehicle testing
    • Functional safety / diagnostics
  • Experience translating OEM/customer requirements into battery system specifications and engineering targets.
  • Proven ability to solve complex system-level problems involving multiple engineering disciplines.
  • Strong technical communication skills and ability to work directly with OEM engineering organizations.
  • Experience with Rivian, Lucid, Tesla, Ford, GM, Stellantis, or other EV/OEM battery programs is highly valued.

The Profile We Value

We are particularly interested in engineers who have moved beyond a single component or discipline and can think across the complete battery system.

The ideal candidate can answer questions such as:

What does the vehicle need? → What must the battery system deliver? → What does that mean for the pack, cells, BMS, thermal system and validation strategy?

You should be comfortable taking ownership of ambiguous system-level problems, bringing the right technical teams together, making engineering trade-offs, and driving issues through resolution.

Why This Role

This role offers the opportunity to move beyond ownership of an individual subsystem and have broader influence over battery system architecture, performance, customer integration, and technical decision-making.

As Gotion expands its North American engineering capability, strong performers will have the opportunity to take broader technical ownership, mentor and build engineering capability, and help define how our EV battery systems organization operates.

Gotion Inc. is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to fostering a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve, cultivating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and ensuring equal employment opportunities for all.

We provide equal opportunity to all individuals regardless of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related conditions (including breastfeeding), parental status, criminal histories consistent with legal requirements, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Freight Analyst Intern
description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented and analytical Freight Analyst Intern to support our logistics operations. The primary goal of this role is to control transportation costs, audit freight invoices, and prevent duplicate shipping charges. Please submit your resume, a brief cover letter outlining your Freight Analyst achievements and any relevant case studies or dashboards you’ve built.

Duties and Responsibilities

Freight Bill Audit & Cost Control

 Review and audit freight invoices from carriers, warehouses, and third-party logistics providers.

 Verify billing accuracy against approved rates, shipment records, and service agreements.

 Identify duplicate freight charges, billing errors, overcharges, and unauthorized fees.

 Analyze parcel, LTL, FTL, and fulfillment shipping costs to identify savings opportunities.

Shipping Operations

 Track shipping performance, transit times, damages, and delivery exceptions.

 Ensure no duplicate shipments or unnecessary reshipments occur.

 Evaluate carrier performance and recommend routing improvements.

 Identify trends, root causes, and operational inefficiencies through data analysis.

 Develop SOPs and internal controls to improve logistics and inventory accuracy.

Basic Requirements

 Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering (IE), Supply Chain, Analytics, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

 Experience in logistics, inventory control, operations, or analytics preferred.

 Experience with Amazon FBA / multi-warehouse operations.

 Knowledge of parcel, LTL, FTL, eCommerce fulfillment, and carrier management.

 Computer proficiency with Google Suite and advanced skills in Microsoft Excel including Pivot Tables, formulas, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and data modeling.

 Proven experience in freight bill audit, shipping cost analysis, and inventory management.

 Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to perform in a fast-moving environment.

 Understanding of emerging supply chain technologies such as automation, AI tools, and traceability systems preferred.

What We Offer

 High visibility role with direct impact on company growth

 Opportunity to work closely with leadership team

 Career growth into operations / supply chain leadership

 Opportunities for professional growth and ongoing training

 Collaborative, inclusive team culture with a focus on work-life balance

description:
Role Organization

Role Title: Network Engineer Team Lead

Team: Project Services

Reporting to: Network Team Manager

Company Overview

At NetCov, we specialize in delivering cutting-edge IT and cybersecurity solutions designed to protect and optimize the digital infrastructure for the industries we serve. We differentiate ourselves through deep knowledge of our clients’ business and a commitment to exceptional service.

About the Role

As a senior member of the Project Services Team, the Network Engineer Team Lead architects and implements complex network infrastructures across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments (Azure, AWS), partnering with the Network Architect on solution design and review, while leading and developing the network engineering function. The role combines deep technical expertise with leadership: setting standards, mentoring engineers, and ensuring consistent, high-quality delivery.

Serving as the technical authority for all network engagements, the Team Lead is accountable for quality, documentation, and risk management, and for resolving advanced networking issues across the client base, taking projects from inception to production and end-user attestation.

Technical Responsibilities
  • Architect and implement complex on-premises, virtual, and cloud (AWS/Azure) network infrastructures, taking projects from inception through production and end-user attestation.
  • Partner with the Network Team Architect to design, review, and validate network solutions prior to implementation.
  • Troubleshoot network-impacting outages quickly and efficiently in unfamiliar environments, with minimal client impact.
  • Implement and support advanced routing (OSPF, BGP, VRRP, HSRP), L2 technologies (STP variants, 802.1x, 802.1ad), and core services (DHCP, DNS, RADIUS/NPS).
  • Design and troubleshoot VPN and tunneling technologies, including SSL/TLS, IPSEC, policy-based VPNs, and GRE.
  • Work hands-on in the CLI across Cisco, Palo Alto, SonicWall, Meraki, Fortinet, Aruba, and Ruckus platforms.
  • Standardize and maintain accurate documentation of client network environments before handoff to support teams.
Leadership Responsibilities
  • Provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring, and coaching to network engineers and project resources from technical oversight
  • Review network designs, implementation plans, and documentation before client delivery.
  • Serve as the senior escalation point for complex networking challenges and lead high-visibility engagements.
  • Identify risks early, drive process improvement and automation, and partner with the Engineering, Escalations, and Service Desk teams on seamless handoffs.
  • Support the Network Team Manager with interviews and hiring of the network engineers.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required
  • Experience:3-5 years of high-level, hands-on networking experience, ideally within an MSP or multi-client environment.
  • Networking:Deep expertise in the TCP/IP stack, L2/L3 forwarding, advanced routing (OSPF, BGP, VRRP, HSRP), and L2 technologies (STP, 802.1x, 802.1ad).
  • Services & Security:Hands-on with DHCP, DNS, RADIUS (NPS), and VPN/tunneling (SSL/TLS, IPSEC, GRE).
  • Vendor Platforms:CLI-level experience with Cisco, Palo Alto, SonicWall, Meraki, Fortinet, Aruba, and Ruckus.
  • Cloud:Strong understanding of AWS and Azure networking.
  • Leadership & Communication:Proven ability to mentor engineers, set standards, and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Certifications:Cisco CCNA or greater, AWS Solutions Architect, and/or Azure Network Engineer certification (or similar) preferred.

Role Logistics

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.
  • This position may require travel to clients or company offices as needed.

description:

Secret - Current

At Raytheon, the foundation of everything we do is rooted in our values and a higher calling – to help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression. We bring the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. Our team solves tough, meaningful problems that create a safer, more secure world.

Join the Team Behind the Final Line of Defense

The LPWS—derived from the U.S. Navy’s renowned Phalanx Close‑In Weapon System (CIWS)—brings that same trusted protection to the land domain, delivering unmatched defense against rockets, artillery, and mortar (RAM) threats. It safeguards friendly forces and critical assets precisely when the stakes are highest.

Equipping U.S. warfighters and allied forces with proven Terminal Defense Systems, the LPWS serves as the final layer of protection and a powerful deterrent against incoming threats.

Originally engineered to defend ships from missiles and aerial attacks, the system was expertly adapted by the Army to protect ground forces and vital infrastructure from indirect fire threats, including rockets, mortars, and artillery shells.

Built for reliability. Designed for mission success. Driven by performance.

Our Field Engineering team is seeking Electronics Test & Integration Field Technician(s) to provide field service support. In this role you perform comprehensive troubleshooting and repair of circuit cards, cable harnesses, electronic assemblies, and electro‑optical systems.

This unaccompanied role is a rotational deployment to CENTCOM OCONUS locations for extended terms with additional compensation.

When not on deployment this role will be Onsite at Fort Sill, OK with availability for assignments to various CONUS / OCONUS sites.

Onboarding and training are conducted at Fort Sill, OK.

Relocation Assistance is available.


Employment is contingent upon meeting all medical requirements for overseas assignments including comprehensive post-offer medical examination.

What You Will Do

  • Analyze equipment failures to determine root causes and recommend effective corrective actions.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert, providing technical guidance and support as needed.
  • Evaluate, assess, and deliver training to force protection personnel on all system configurations.
  • Inspect, test, and align designated systems to ensure compliance with required specifications.
  • Utilize schematics, drawings, specifications, and General Purpose Electrical/Electronic Test Equipment (GPETE) to diagnose and repair system and equipment faults.
  • Deliver up‑to‑date training on system operation, maintenance, alignment, and repair.
  • Support the acquisition of OEM technical data (drawings, test data, etc.) through appropriate channels.
  • Develop and support installation, maintenance, repair, and operation procedures for communications and electro‑optical equipment.
  • Evaluate and document field operational capability, reporting results to customers and program leadership.
  • Perform routine system maintenance and computer system administrative functions, including analysis of system operations.
  • Perform other technical duties as assigned.


Qualifications You Must Have

  • Typically requires a Bachelor’s and a minimum of 5+ years prior relevant experience, or an Associate’s Degree in a related field and a minimum of 7+ years’ experience.
  • Proficient with standard electronic assembly and testing tools.
  • Experience testing and validating electromechanical systems using diagnostic equipment such as spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, and voltmeters, or similar systems.
  • Strong troubleshooting, repair, and testing skills across a wide range of electronic components and systems.
  • Experience detecting, isolating, and correcting faults in computer systems and peripheral devices.
  • Hands‑on experience with systems integration, software, and electromechanical systems.
  • Active and transferable U.S. government issued SECRET security clearance or INTERIM Clearance is required prior to start date.
  • U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.


Qualifications We Prefer

  • Relevant experience may substitute for a degree.
  • Prior field experience or military service with land‑based weapon systems.
  • Skilled in maintaining, troubleshooting, and supporting combat control and weapon systems.
  • Experience testing and adjusting weapon firing, guidance, and launch systems.
  • Proficient in maintaining gyroscopes, sights, and electro‑optical fire control components.
  • Ability to inspect, test, calibrate, and repair advanced microcomputers, radar systems, and data display units.
  • Working knowledge of electro‑optical sensor hardware/software and military/commercial electronics maintenance practices.
  • Ability to install, diagnose, and repair servomotors and closed‑loop feedback systems for fire control, sensors, antenna gimbals, and remote weapon systems.
  • Familiarity with military protocols, operating systems, and database administration.
  • Advanced CIWS military training.
  • Strong planning, scheduling, and execution abilities.
  • Able to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.


Special Work Conditions

  • Extensive travel will be required; up to 100% to include other international destinations.
  • Some locations will be in the middle east desert with temperatures above 120 degrees F.
  • Willing and able to deploy to remote international locations with little notification.
  • Willing and able to deploy to environments that may include harsh living conditions (extreme heat and cold, deployed living conditions and / or hostile work environment.
  • Willing and able to move and / or transport weights such as test equipment, ladders, instruments, and cable reels weighing up to 60 pounds using proper lifting techniques or material moving equipment.
  • Willing and able to work 12-16 hours a day and be on call 24/7.
  • Willing and able to traverse platforms.
  • Willing and able to work in a bivouac environment.
  • Willing and able to travel over rough, uneven terrain.


What We Offer

Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.

description:

This role is critical to driving innovation, market expansion and customer success, supporting biopharmaceutical manufacturing, protein purification, and downstream processing applications, within our Chromatography business unit portfolio. You will collaborate with R&D, manufacturing, regulatory, and commercial teams to deliver high-performance solutions that meet the evolving needs of biologics developers and manufacturers.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Product Leadership

  • Define and execute the product roadmap for affinity ligands and chromatography resins, aligned with market trends and customer needs in bioprocessing.
  • Conduct market analysis and engage with key opinion leaders to identify opportunities for innovation and differentiation.
  • Develop business cases for new product development, including resin formats, ligand technologies, and application-specific solutions

Product Development & Lifecycle Management

  • Translate voice of customer and market research into new product opportunities
  • Collaborate with R&D and process development teams to ensure product performance, scalability, and regulatory compliance (e.g., GMP, ISO).
  • Manage product lifecycle from concept through launch and post-market optimization, including phase-out strategies.

Commercial Enablement & Growth

  • Partner with marketing and sales to develop go-to-market strategies, technical content, and training materials.
  • Lead pricing, positioning, and promotional campaigns tailored to different customer segments
  • Monitor product performance, customer feedback, and competitive landscape to drive continuous improvement.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Serve as the internal expert on the chromatography business, supporting commercial activities and customer engagements.
  • Work closely with quality, and supply chain teams to ensure product availability, quality, compliance and operational excellence.
  • Represent the product line at industry conferences, webinars, and customer meetings.

Education and Work Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, or related field (MBA preferred).
  • 7+ years of product management experience in life sciences, with a focus on chromatography, purification technologies, or bioprocessing.
  • 2-3+ years of direct report management experience
  • Good understanding of chromatography and downstream processing workflows
  • Experience working in regulated environments (e.g., GMP, ISO 9001).
  • Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills.
  • Proficient in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project and Visio)
  • Customer facing experience and the ability to build mutually beneficial, trusting relationships with internal and external stakeholders
  • Strong attention to detail with excellent verbal and written communication skills

Our mission is to inspire advances in bioprocessing as a trusted partner in the production of biologic drugs that improve human health worldwide. At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. We deliver solutions that help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression, creating a safer, more secure world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

The Mechanical Analysis and Test (MA&T) Department is responsible for ensuring structural and thermal design robustness across the Raytheon portfolio of products. From preliminary concepts to fielded weapon system support, MA&T delivers innovative structural and thermal engineering solutions utilizing methods ranging from classical fundamental & empirically based techniques to state-of-the-art finite element methods leveraging industry leading commercial tools; all complimented and validated by tests executed in a manner to ensure cost effective yet technically balanced solutions.

The Senior Thermal Analyst position is located in Marlborough, MA and the role is onsite.

As a mid-level career Senior Thermal Analyst you will be responsible for detailed thermal analysis on products throughout their lifecycle from initial design trade studies and proposals through qualification testing to enduring production support. The analysis will cover a wide range of difficult problems, requiring solutions that are imaginative, thorough, practicable, and consistent with organization objectives. The analysis tasks will span the spectrum from classical hand analyses to detailed analyses requiring the use of finite element analysis software. A Thermal Engineer of this salary grade is expected to have a level of technical competence with thermodynamic principles. The Thermal Engineer will be held accountable for completing his/her work within the agreed upon cost and schedule. Additionally, the selected candidate will be expected to present their work for peer reviews and to be a peer reviewer for other engineers’ work. Finally, the engineer is expected to plan and support tests, perform data reduction and engage in thermal model correlation.

What You Will Do

  • Perform Hand Calculations to determine scope of higher detail analysis models
  • Perform detailed thermal analyses to solve various program thermal challenges
  • Generate test plans required to validate analyses and verify hardware compliance to customer requirements
  • Analyze test data to validate and correlate models
  • Work with experienced analysts on problems of moderate complexity to provide the answers needed under program cost and schedule constraints
  • Review your work with peers to ensure technical accuracy
  • Present results to internal, external, and government customers
  • Generate detailed documentation of work and archive for reference
  • Act as a technical leader (help define/refine and/or develop MA&T department technical processes and tools) and/or lead analysis/test teams


Qualifications You Must Have

  • Typically requires a degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) and a minimum of 5 years of prior relevant experience unless prohibited by local laws/regulations.
  • Experience in thermal analysis with any of the following tools: FloTHERM, PATRAN, Thermal Desktop/SINDA or ANSYS or equivalent
  • Experience in mechanical principles to solve classical thermal analysis solutions both inside and outside of finite element tools and an ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities
  • Ability to obtain a U.S. government issued security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance, Clearance must be active and transferable prior to start date
  • Demonstrated experience in thermal testing: Planning, organization, execution, data reduction and correlation


Qualifications We Prefer

  • Degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering
  • 5+ years of professional experience in the thermal analysis of complex systems that require collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines
  • Experience with solid modeling CAD tools such as CREO or equivalent
  • Experience in Electronics Cooling and Aerodynamic Heating Analyses
  • Experience presenting to external customers
  • Demonstrated experience in leading a team of thermal analysts on program efforts
  • Demonstrated experience in leading thermal testing, including model correlation
  • Ability to travel to government and other facilities in support of program activities
  • Advanced degree in aforementioned disciplines. ABET is the preferred, although not required, accreditation standard

title: Channel Solution Architect (Remote)
description:

We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. Join the CrowdStrike mission to stop breaches as a technical expert working with our largest and most strategic partners.

title: Director, Global Export Controls & Technical Governance
description:
Job Posting Title:

Director, Global Export Controls & Technical Governance

Req ID:

10156966

Job Description:

Director, Global Export Controls & Technical Governance

Role Overview

The Director, Global Export Controls & Technical Governance serves as the principal corporate authority over the enterprise export control framework, holding ultimate functional accountability for identifying, segmenting, and mitigating national security, dual-use technology, and geopolitical compliance risks across all business units. Operating within the IC@D Enterprise Standards, this executive leader is the principal architect designing and maintaining a resilient, scalable compliance architecture benchmarked against adjacent technology sectors to ensure corporate operations maintain strict regulatory defensibility while leveraging automation to support advanced product development, Imagineering, and project delivery worldwide.

This position exercises direct oversight over the centralized export control tower, establishing core compliance guardrails for dual-use technology, restricted party screening, international technical data transfers, and sanctions/embargos. The Director leads a team consisting of automated systems compliance, transactional execution, and advisory tracks, ensuring that sourcing and engineering teams, technology developers, and decentralized trade champions execute day-to-day workflows with absolute precision. This role serves as a mission-critical corporate partner supporting the legal transfer of products and technology across all Disney segments and geographies, protecting the brand's global integrity, and acting as the primary functional advisor to executive leadership, the Integrity and Compliance team, and Legal/Technical resources across the enterprise. The Director, Global Export Controls & Technical Governance, reports directly to the Executive Director, Global Trade Services and Customs Operations.

Scope & Impact

The Director possesses high-visibility corporate executive presence, interfacing regularly with senior leadership across the company and across the globe. This role actively consults across a myriad of functions, business segments, and international regions to ensure known compliance gaps are mitigated, and permanent internal controls and training are put in place to avoid these issues in the future. Primary internal clients and consulting nodes include:

  • Walt Disney Imagineering (WDI): Direct advisory support and risk mitigation for WDI Ride Engineering, Research & Development (R&D), and Creative Technology teams across the Burbank/Glendale and Zurich hubs to secure intangible tech transfers, access controls, and Technology Control Plans (TCP) for entities moving specialized equipment and controlled assets around the world.

  • Studio & Production Technology: Early-stage integration with motion picture and theatrical production crews, streaming media engineering groups, and digital asset management centers to govern physical shipments, software creation and distribution pipelines.

  • Disney Cruise Line & Parks Logistics: Upstream compliance mapping with global supply chain management to facilitate the legal, compliant, and accelerated cross-border transport of specialized engineering equipment, ride components, and marine provisions.

  • Corporate Legal Services: Direct alignment and routine risk-profiling and mitigation with the Integrity and Compliance team and senior legal leadership.

  • Global Footprint & Regions: Strategic cross-border oversight spanning the Americas, EMEA, and APAC theaters, establishing standard execution workflows revising procedures and screening rules to reduce compliance friction and facilitate legal trade worldwide.

Key Responsibilities

  • Formulate and execute the long-term enterprise export controls strategy and mandatory governance standards, authoring the Trade Component of the Disney Code of Conduct, comprehensive Corporate Export Policies and Procedures, and core compliance protocols across all global footprints in partnership with Integrity and Compliance @Disney.

  • Govern the Hub-and-Spoke Matrix Operating Model by establishing standardized operational KPIs, communication cadences, and compliance metrics for decentralized segment Trade Champions to ensure consistent adherence to export controls across all Lines of Business.

  • Mandate, design, and oversee the global systemic screening of suppliers, vendors, and customers across the entire enterprise, ensuring compliance for every business partner appearing on any corporate contract or agreement.

  • Provide strategic leadership and direction to the multi-functional export control tower, maintaining direct oversight of separate tracks: the Senior Manager, Automation & Systems Governance (Architecture/Environment) and the Manager, Global Export Network & Operational Compliance (Transactional/Advisory).

  • Partner directly with IC@D to interpret complex export control, technology transfer, and sanctions changes, translating macro geopolitical shifts into executable enterprise standards embedded early in business planning and technology design. Create proactive internal controls and address/close historical control gaps.

  • Lead trade education initiatives across Disney by sponsoring the creation of awareness, proficiency and expert training, partnering directly with the Integrity and Compliance team to deploy training across all geographies and learning vehicles.

  • Maintain enterprise-wide export control audit readiness and oversee the internal trade self-assessment schedule, partnering with IC@D and Internal Audit to conduct the reviews, address findings, resolve systemic risks, and drive long-term remediation priorities.

  • Accountable for compliance automation review and approve workflows and system (screening) configurations in close partnership with the Global Trade Automation & Data Governance team.

  • Serve as the senior functional escalation point and chief authority for high-risk export control match resolutions, complex technology transfer authorizations, restricted party hits, and critical cross-border compliance concerns.

Basic Qualifications

  • 15+ years of progressive corporate experience directing export compliance frameworks, global trade compliance, international technical transfers (tangible/intangible), or corporate regulatory auditing within a large public multinational enterprise.

  • Leadership experience managing software lifecycles, technical professionals, and multi-layered compliance networks across a highly matrixed global commercial footprint.

  • Comprehensive technical knowledge of U.S. and international export control regimes, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions, and technology transfer protocols.

Preferred Education

  • BA/BS in International Business or Economics preferred. Ideal candidate will have be a Certified Export Specialist.

The hiring range for this position in Glendale, CA is $185,000.00-$226,000.00 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

TITLE: Senior Managing Director, In-Service Program Implementation

TEAM: Program Implementation, Corps Program and Leadership Experiences, CMLD

REPORTS TO: VP, CPLE

LOCATION: Flexible/Remote

PRIORITY DEADLINE: August 26. Applications submitted after the deadline will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

THE ROLE

The Senior Managing Director, In-Service Program Implementation on the CMLD team is obsessed with building corps members’ teacher leadership during their two year CM journey. The ideal candidate is focused on building an experience that prepares CMs with the pedagogical and leadership skills to achieve impact and build lifelong connections across the TFA network. They are responsible for planning and leading the implementation of direct-to-CM programs, specifically In-Service experiences.

The ideal candidate is a vision-centered leader who deeply understands how to craft and design key moment experiences for corps members and staff. They can develop a detailed strategy aligned to Teach For America’s program model, Theory of Leadership, of 2CM Point of View. From there, they are able to execute that strategy for the full corps while building relationships and influencing a broad range of stakeholders. They will need to be dogged about achieving the vision for the in-service experience(s), while also providing capacity across the team on various strategies. They will need to be an exceptional project and cross-functional people manager who can provide clear metrics, direction, and deliverables to key stakeholders across the organization. They must have a unique balance of focus and flexibility and lead with equal parts strategy and relationships. They also ensure program implementation success across the team by providing additional capacity to meet various strategic needs.

The SMD, In-Service Program Implementation will report to the VP, CPLE, collaborate with the CMLD team, and manage laterally and cross functionally to plan and execute In-Service key moment(s).

WEEK IN THE LIFE

Over the course of any week, the SMD, In-Service Program Implementation will spend time:

  • Leverage our 2CM POV to map out key moments in the participant journey and set a vision for an aligned 2CM leadership experience

  • Meeting with subject-matter experts teams, such as the Learning & Insights team, to build out a clear, aligned learning agenda for the experience that allows the team to iterate year-over-year

  • Partner across CMLD to design and plan the experience, in alignment with the experience vision, ensuring strong staffing plans, operations, session materials, and facilitation

  • Partner closely with regional and hub teams to ensure the local contextualization and implementation of the In-Service key moment, in alignment with a regional support strategy for In-Service

  • Engage in design sprints to determine regional needs and develop off-the-shelf resources and tools

  • Project manage the CPLE team toward key In-Service milestones

  • Facilitate staff training so that the experiences outcomes are clear to all staff who execute the program

THE PERSON

(45%) ARCHITECT AND STEWARD KEY MOMENTS IN THE CORPS EXPERIENCE. Plan and manage complex projects during our CM’s in-service experience. Work alongside multiple layers of stakeholders, including corps members, students, and staff, resulting in a strong CM experience(s) and key moment(s) during In-Service and gaining insights into adaptations to the program in future years. Create a vision, align a strategy and manage the execution of In-Service key moment(s) that are both centrally and regionally facilitated while ensuring seamless integration across workstreams, such as operations, staffing, and program.

(20%) SET VISION & DIRECTION AND CONTRIBUTE TO A STRONG TEAM CULTURE. Steward the In-Service key moment(s) by leveraging key stakeholders and managing cross-functionally/laterally toward outcomes. Provide the broader team with clarity, as well as the tools, resources, and support to plan and execute the key moment(s). Project manage key stakeholders toward results. Flow capacity where needed and serve as a true utility player.

(25%) PARTNER ACROSS REGIONAL AND NATIONAL TEAMS. The Corps Program and Leadership Experiences team is responsible for designing and executing key moment experiences that demonstrate the strength and breadth of our national network and the power of localized, contextual experiences. As such, the SMD, In-Service Program Implementation plays an essential leadership role in ensuring a strong central program experience and the local implementation of that experience. This requires strong coordination across central teams, a thorough regional support plan, and eye toward execution. Support the maintenance of strong integrated partnerships with subject-matter experts to bring the strength and gifts of our national movement to bear on behalf of our corps members, while also creating and maintaining meaningful partnerships with local teams to ensure regions are equipped and supported to contextualize the experience. Establish impactful external partnerships to ensure that corps members have access to authentic experiences, and best-in-class resources.

(10%) FLOW CAPACITY TO MEET VARIOUS NEEDS across CMLD towards the end of optimizing program. Operate as a key member of the CPLE team and identify risks and opportunities to use the team’s gifts and capacity for short-term projects.

THE MUST HAVES

Prior Experience:

  • 8-10 years of aligned experience, inclusive of roles requiring direct management and strong lateral management, relationship building, and cross-functional leadership.

  • Significant experience designing, executing, and leading large-scale key moments in alignment with Teach For America’s program model

  • Experience leading regional program

Work Demands:

  • Ability to work weekends and evenings, as necessary

  • Occasional travel may be required

Skills

  • Ability to set and evolve vision and direction for key moments and leadership experiences

  • Ability to build strong relationships with others in challenging situations

  • Knack for influencing others toward outcomes through sophisticated relationship management

  • Ability to make timely decisions and demonstrate good judgment

  • Ability to constantly improve and learn from past experiences

  • Ability to inspire and motivate others to perform against measurable goals

THE TEAM

The Corps Program and Leadership Experiences (CPLE) team is responsible for designing and implementing innovative leadership development experiences that shape the most critical moments in the Teach For America corps member journey. Within this team, Program Implementation serves as the engine that brings these experiences to life by leading the execution of high-impact learning experiences, beginning with Pre-Service and expanding across the broader corps member continuum. The team partners deeply across national and regional functions to ensure corps members experience development opportunities that are ambitious, cohesive, and responsive to local context. Team members operate at the intersection of strategy, implementation, and cross-functional leadership, translating vision into exceptional execution at scale. Together, we are reimagining how transformative leadership development experiences prepare corps members to lead lasting change for students and communities.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

The applicable salary range for each U.S.-based role is based on where the employee works and is aligned to one of 3 tiers according to a cost of labor index in that geographic area. Starting pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. New hires are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint depending on qualifications, internal equity, and the budgeted amount for the role. The expected salary range for this role are set forth below. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)

As a not-for-profit healthcare organization, Presbyterian Healthcare Services may qualify eligible physicians for the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.

National Health Service Corps (NHSC) Loan Repayment Program

Physicians practicing at eligible sites may qualify for federal student loan repayment through the National Health Service Corps program, providing up to $75,000 in tax-free loan repayment for a two-year service commitment at an approved site in a designated shortage area.

Participation is competitive and subject to federal approval and funding availability.

New Mexico Physician Tax Credit

Eligible physicians practicing in New Mexico may qualify for a state income tax credit of up to $10,000 annually based on program requirements.

Eligibility and certification are determined by the State of New Mexico.

New Mexico Health Professional Loan Repayment Program

Physicians working in designated shortage areas may qualify for state-funded student loan assistance of up to $75,000 annually through an approved service commitment.

Participation is competitive and subject to state approval and funding availability.

New Mexico is the first state in the nation to provide no-cost childcare for eligible families, creating meaningful support for working parents.

Program highlights include:

  • Coverage options that may include infant and toddler care, preschool, before- and after-school programs, and summer childcare

Eligibility and participation requirements are determined by the State of New Mexico.

New Mexico Opportunity Scholarship

New Mexico residents may be eligible for the Opportunity Scholarship, which can cover up to 100% of tuition and required fees at participating public colleges and universities.

The program supports both recent graduates and adult learners pursuing educational opportunities.

Eligibility and award determinations are made by the State of New Mexico and participating institutions.

title: Analista Sênior de Crédito e Risco
description:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.

We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Analista Sênior de Crédito e Risco

O que um(a) Analista Sênior de Crédito e Risco bem-sucedido(a) faz na Fiserv?
Na Fiserv, este(a) profissional atua de forma estratégica para proteger o negócio, apoiar o crescimento sustentável e fortalecer a relação com clientes por meio de decisões de crédito e risco bem fundamentadas. Seu foco está na prevenção da inadimplência, na renegociação estruturada e na recuperação de crédito, sempre equilibrando risco, experiência do cliente e resultado financeiro. Em parceria com diferentes áreas, transforma dados, indicadores e contexto de mercado em ações práticas e escaláveis. Também contribui para evoluir estratégias, processos e automações que aumentam a eficiência da operação.

O que você vai fazer:

  • Analisar carteiras, indicadores e comportamentos de crédito e risco para identificar sinais iniciais de inadimplência e definir ações preventivas
  • Desenvolver e aplicar estratégias de renegociação de contratos com clientes pessoa jurídica, buscando recuperação de crédito e sustentabilidade da relação comercial
  • Avaliar cenários de risco, perda potencial e viabilidade de negociação, recomendando tratativas adequadas entre renegociação, cobrança estruturada ou encaminhamento jurídico
  • Conduzir análises de crédito e contencioso com foco em recuperação de ativos, cláusulas contratuais, aceleração de vencimento e medidas de mitigação
  • Propor e executar réguas de cobrança, campanhas e disparos massivos de comunicação para ampliar eficiência na recuperação e no relacionamento com clientes
  • Apoiar iniciativas de automação e uso de inteligência artificial em processos de cobrança, monitoramento e tomada de decisão
  • Acompanhar a aderência de motores, regras e estratégias de crédito sob a perspectiva de performance, risco e efetividade operacional
  • Interagir com áreas internas e liderança para recomendar ações, priorizar medidas de recuperação e apoiar decisões estratégicas da operação

title: Anesthesia Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY

This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

The Anesthesia Technician is responsible for clinically supporting the activities of the Department of Anesthesia. Activities include: provision of supplies and equipment as well as performing a variety of tasks including indirect patient care that help ensure the safe and cost effective delivery of anesthetic patient care.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.

Employees must abide by all Joint Commission Requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, patient care, patient rights and ethical treatment, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety and quality programs, sustaining compliance with National Patient Safety Goals, and licensure and health screenings.

Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the hospital's policies and procedures, including its Service Standards and its Code of Conduct.

* Actively participates in quality control, quality assurance and preventative maintenance activities.
* Assists in the evaluation of new products by providing feedback regarding use.
* Assists with record keeping and patient charges.
* Assures replacement or repair of malfunctioning equipment.
* Attends and participates in equipment and supply inservices, evaluations, and staff meetings.
* Contributes in a positive manner to unit and department; supports team culture.
* Correctly checks and sets up all equipment and supplies utilized by the Department of Anesthesia including anesthesia machines, monitors, invasive lines, non-controlled pharmaceuticals and other tasks as requested by Anesthesia.
* Identifies and shares recommendations for containing costs in assigned area.
* Maintains an effective working relationship with staff, managers, physicians, patients and their families.
* Maintains and services equipment by cleaning, and if requested, by sterilizing, assembling, and testing, troubleshooting, requisitioning and receiving of inspections and maintenance.
* May assist the anesthesia provider with intra-operative fluid management including volume resuscitation.
* Participates in the monitoring and documenting of quality improvement issues
* Participates on unit, department or hospital committees as requested.
* Performs housekeeping/stocking duties in order to maintain a clean, safe work environment.
* Practices aseptic techniques according to established standards of care and infection control policies.
* Prepares and maintains patient monitoring devices and anesthesia delivery systems before, during and after anesthesia.
* Prepares and operates auto transfusion equipment.
* Proactively uses the problem solving process to identify, prevent or resolve inter-or intra-departmental problems.
* Properly disposes of non-controlled pharmaceuticals.
* Responsible for self-assessment of skill level and seeking resources to learn new skills, equipment, or procedures to maintain currency in position.
* Supports administrative decisions and assures implementation and compliance with all department, institutional and regulatory policies and procedures.
* Works with clinical educator to orient new staff members and students to the role of anesthesia technician as requested.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities as well as possession of any required licenses or certifications is qualifying.

Education: High School Diploma or GED equivalent.

Experience: One (1) year of directly related work experience.

License/Certification:

  • RQI Healthcare Provider Basic Life Support
  • or
  • Basic Life Support by American Heart Association (AHA)

KNOWLEDGE

These are the observable and measurable attributes and skills required to perform successfully the essential functions of the job and are generally demonstrated through qualifying experience, education or licensure/certification.

* Ability to be flexible in assignments.
* Ability to learn and evaluate new equipment and procedures quickly.
* Ability to provide appropriate care based on the needs of the individual taking into consideration age, culture, and developmental issues.
* Ability to respond with flexibility to unusual and emergent situations, remain calm in stressful and emergency situations.
* Ability to speak, read, write, and understand English effectively at a level appropriate for the job.
* Ability to work independently and prioritize duties during time of stress.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with individuals of diverse cultural backgrounds.
* Knowledge of location, operation, calibration, and maintenance of anesthesia equipment and supplies.
* Knowledge of operating room procedures, aseptic techniques and infection control policies.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The Physical Requirements and Working Conditions in which the job is typically performed are available from the Occupational Health Department. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

Pay Range
Compensation is based on the level and requirements of the role.
Salary within our ranges may also be determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, location, and abilities, as required by the role, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
Typically, new team members join at the minimum to mid salary range.

The Building Delivery Manager is the Client focal point responsible for safe, timely and quality delivery of assigned project buildings and associated facilities, from engineering and procurement through construction, pre-commissioning, commissioning support and handover.
The role provides delivery assurance, supervision and close follow-up of contractors, coordinates multidisciplinary interfaces, identifies blockers early, and drives clear corrective actions with owners and due dates to protect schedule, HSE, quality and handover readiness.

  • Site-based role with daily interface with construction, engineering, procurement, planning, HSE, QA/QC, commissioning and operations representatives.
  • Covers end-to-end delivery of assigned buildings, including engineering maturity, procurement readiness, construction progress, quality control, HSE performance, pre-commissioning and commissioning readiness.
  • Lead weekly multidisciplinary meetings and ensure decisions, actions, owners and due dates are recorded and followed until closure.
  • Escalates delivery risks, blockers and deviations through factual reporting and recommended management actions.
  • Maintain a consolidated view of delivery status for assigned buildings from engineering through commissioning handover.
  • Follow up contractors' mobilization, staffing, site organization, workface readiness and execution priorities.
  • Track engineering deliverables, technical queries, approvals, design maturity and field engineering support required for construction continuity.
  • Monitor procurement and material availability for equipment, bulk materials, construction packages and subcontracted scopes affecting site progress.
  • Monitor construction execution, productivity, progress measurement, look-ahead planning, constraints and recovery actions.
  • Verify that HSE requirements are understood and implemented, with prompt follow-up of observations, incidents and corrective actions.
  • Verify quality implementation, including inspection readiness, NCR management, punch list closure and compliance with approved specifications and procedures.
  • Coordinate construction completion, mechanical completion, system prioritization and handover sequence with commissioning stakeholders.
  • Provide concise reporting to Client management on schedule, progress, risks, HSE, quality, blockers, contractor performance and required decisions.

  • Significant experience in building, infrastructure, industrial facilities or EPC project delivery, preferably in oil and gas, LNG, petrochemical or heavy industrial projects.
  • Strong multidisciplinary coordination experience covering engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning interfaces.
  • Demonstrated ability to challenge contractor plans, identify delivery risks and drive timely corrective actions.
  • Good understanding of HSE, QA/QC, construction planning, progress measurement and mechanical completion principles.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to report clearly, escalate factually and coordinate stakeholders without direct line authority.
  • Site-based mindset, hands-on follow-up and strong discipline in action tracking and closure.

Place of work : Sohar, Oman

title: Senior Director of Spacecraft Components
description:
About the role

Muon seeks an experienced leader to build and guide our Spacecraft Components organization through our next stage of rapid growth. This organization designs, qualifies, and delivers the components at the heart of every Muon spacecraft across three subteams: Electronics & Embedded (avionics, power electronics, RF, and electrical test), Modules & Mechanisms (integrated modules and actuation mechanisms, plus design support to our instrument and propulsion teams), and Solar & Deployables (solar arrays and deployable systems). The role reports to Muon's Senior Director of Hardware Engineering.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned, cross-disciplinary leader experienced at organizing and scaling rapidly growing teams, with strong program management skills. Experience designing and manufacturing low-volume, high-mix products efficiently is a must.

This role is split between our San Jose and Mountain View locations, with the expectation of regular onsite days at both.

Responsibilities

  • Lead a multidisciplinary organization to architect, design, qualify, and deliver a catalog of spacecraft components — electronics, RF, integrated modules and mechanisms, and solar and deployable systems — serving a wide range of missions
  • Own component roadmaps that balance the needs of concurrent missions and platform evolution, driving standardization and reuse across spacecraft platforms
  • Own component-level design, analysis, qualification, and electrical test strategies, partnering with Hardware Reliability & Test to ensure consistent qualification across the catalog
  • Provide engineering design support to instrument and propulsion teams through the Modules & Mechanisms team
  • Collaborate with Product, Business Development, Systems Engineering, Software, and Operations to ensure components meet the needs of our growing mission portfolio; support proposals and cost models
  • Partner with Production and Supply Chain to scale components from prototype builds to constellation quantities, designing for manufacturability and test
  • Own budgets, schedules, and delivery milestones for component development programs
  • Mentor and support multiple levels of team managers and enable scalable growth within the organization

Qualifications

  • 15+ years of experience designing and/or managing the design of complex, high-reliability systems that operate in harsh environments (spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, drones, etc.)
  • 8+ years of people management experience, including managing engineers and engineering managers
  • Strong technical foundation spanning electrical, embedded, and mechanical design and analysis
  • Experience designing and manufacturing low-volume, high-mix products efficiently
  • Proven experience managing complex engineering projects from concept to deployment, including budget and schedule management
  • Excellent leadership, program management, communication, and problem-solving skills; excited to work in a fast-paced environment with new challenges each week
  • B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field

Nice-to-have Skills

  • Flight heritage delivering spaceflight avionics, mechanisms, solar arrays, or similar components
  • Experience standing up new teams or reorganizing engineering organizations during rapid growth
  • Experience with vertically integrated hardware development, from in-house design through production at scale
  • Experience with RF hardware or electrical test infrastructure development
  • Experience supporting instrument or propulsion system development

Salary

The salary range for this role is $233,000 - $262,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. The Company may, for legitimate business reasons, decline to pursue any export licensing process.

title: Asset Protection Detective, Gardens - Full Time
location: Palm Beach Gardens, FL, United States
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story.

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Detective, you will help protect company assets, reduce shortage, and support a safe, customer-focused shopping environment. Using surveillance, investigative tools, and strong partnerships with store teams and law enforcement, you will identify and respond to theft, recover merchandise, and help protect our customers, colleagues, and business.

Why This Role Matters

Asset Protection Detectives play an important role in reducing loss while maintaining a safe and welcoming store environment. Through training, observation, investigation, and de-escalation, this role helps protect company assets, support colleagues, and ensure customers can shop with confidence.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

What To Expect

  • Use surveillance techniques, investigative tools, and reporting systems to help identify theft, dishonest activity, and shortage trends.
  • Partner with Asset Protection leaders, store teams, and law enforcement to support investigations and protect company assets.
  • Apply de-escalation tools and sound judgment to help maintain a safe environment for customers and colleagues.
  • Prepare clear documentation, statements, and evidence to support investigations, audits, and legal proceedings.
  • Support team readiness by training colleagues on protocols that help protect company assets.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Help protect customers, colleagues, and company assets by identifying, investigating, and responding to theft and dishonest activity.
  • Use surveillance techniques to support the apprehension of shoplifters and dishonest employees, while following company policies and legal requirements.
  • Recover stolen merchandise and provide statements, evidence, and documentation to support investigations.
  • Prepare timely and accurate reports related to theft incidents, investigations, audits, and assigned activities.
  • Build strong partnerships with store colleagues, Asset Protection leaders, and law enforcement to support investigations and shortage reduction.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, and evidence preservation.
  • Testify in court for criminal and civil cases, as needed.
  • Respond to alarm calls, support special assignments, and facilitate first aid for customers and colleagues when needed.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Ability to observe, identify, and respond to suspicious activity in a retail environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with customers, colleagues, leaders, and law enforcement.

  • Ability to use sound judgment, de-escalation tools, and company procedures to support a safe environment.

  • Ability to handle proprietary, sensitive, and confidential information with discretion and integrity.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail, customer service, asset protection, security, investigations, or law enforcement.

  • Ability to prepare accurate reports, statements, and documentation related to incidents and investigations.

  • Experience using surveillance systems, reporting tools, or investigative technology.

  • Ability to train or coach colleagues on asset protection protocols, shortage reduction, or safety practices.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.
  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department.
  • May occasionally involve reaching above eye level, stooping, kneeling, or crouching.
  • Must be able to apprehend shoplifters.
  • Ability to sustain long periods of time enclosed in surveillance areas.
  • Frequently lift/move up to 30lbs.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!
