title: Social and Behavioral Sciences - Psychology Department - Professor
description:
Wagner College's Division of Social & Behavioral Sciences invites applications for an open-rank, tenure-track faculty position in Criminal Justice beginning in August 2027.

Applicants must possess a Ph.D. in Criminal Justice or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

The successful candidate will play an integral role in the continued growth of Wagner College's Human Services major by supporting its Criminal Justice concentration through teaching, advising, recruitment, and curriculum development.

Candidates should be prepared to teach undergraduate courses including The Criminal Justice System, Criminal Procedure, Criminal Law, Criminology, Law and Society, Introduction to Sociology, and other courses consistent with their expertise and the needs of the department. Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in criminal justice, criminology, criminal law, criminal procedure, law and society, or related areas. Additional teaching responsibilities may be assigned based on the successful candidate's expertise and departmental needs.

In addition to teaching, the faculty member will advise and mentor undergraduate students, contribute to student recruitment and the continued growth of the Human Services major, maintain an active program of scholarship, and participate in departmental, divisional, and college service. Candidates holding a J.D. in addition to a Ph.D. are especially encouraged to apply.

Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching, student mentoring, inclusive pedagogy, and scholarly research. The teaching load is 3/3, with opportunities to teach summer courses.

Wagner College, located in Staten Island, NY, values diversity, equity, and inclusion and encourages applications from candidates whose experiences and perspectives will contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

Application Materials

Applicants should submit the following as a single PDF file under the "Resume" button:

  • Letter of application
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Graduate transcript
  • Statement of teaching philosophy and experience
  • Evidence of teaching excellence (if available)
  • Statement of current and future research plans
  • Contact information for three professional references

Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.

Dr. Laurence Nolan
Interim Division Chair, Social & Behavioral Sciences
Wagner College
LNolan@wagner.edu

title: Senior Automation Scientist/Engineer — Biologics Engineering
description:
Biologics Engineering (BE), part of Oncology R&D, is transforming biologics discovery through the integration of laboratory automation, advanced informatics, and AI. We are building next-generation capabilities to accelerate workflows, improve data quality, and enable smarter scientific decision-making. This is an exciting time for the organization as we create an industry-leading biologics discovery platform that unites scientific excellence, automation, and digital innovation.

We are seeking a Senior Automation Scientist/Engineer to help drive this transformation by embedding laboratory automation and robotics into our workflows and shaping the future of biologics discovery science.

About the Role

The Senior Automation Scientist/Engineer will lead the design, integration, and optimization of robotics, high-throughput systems, and associated data workflows across the BE organization—building solutions that connect instruments, workflow control, data systems, and labware into platforms that are robust, scalable, and operationally sustainable. The successful candidate will bring a strong sense of ownership, taking responsibility for the reliability and long-term performance of our platforms.

Working in a matrix organization, they will partner closely with scientists to understand assay goals, advise on the most effective automation approaches, and translate scientific requirements into fit-for-purpose solutions. Success in this role depends on pairing strong expertise in laboratory automation, scripting, and liquid handling with a clear understanding of the underlying science and how equipment capabilities and design choices affect data quality and reproducibility.

Typical Accountabilities

  • Deliver robust, scalable automation platforms that integrate high-throughput, bench-scale, and related laboratory systems—partnering with scientists to document and map workflows, capture assay requirements, and translate them into fit-for-purpose automation solutions.

  • Serve as the technical authority across multiple automation platforms, scheduling software, and scripting environments—guiding design decisions, resolving complex technical issues, and advising on how equipment capabilities and limitations shape data quality and scientific outcomes.

  • Own the reliability and continuous improvement of shared automation systems and workflows, identifying root causes, driving durable fixes, and raising the operational performance of the platform over time.

  • Support the ongoing operation and troubleshooting of deployed automated workflows to ensure sustained performance and rapid resolution of technical issues.

  • Grow the technical capability of the team by training, mentoring, or supervising junior engineers and scientists, and by influencing scientific thinking and project direction across the automation community and broader stakeholder network.

Qualifications and Skills

Essential

  • Bachelor's or advanced degree in life sciences, engineering, computer science, or a related field, with 4+ years of relevant industry experience.

  • Experience integrating automation with R&D bench science in a biologics, drug discovery, or related life sciences setting.

  • Deep hands-on experience with diverse laboratory automation platforms, liquid handlers, and/or high-throughput analytical technologies. Practical experience with liquid class development and labware definition, evaluation, or optimization.

  • Expertise in automation scheduling software and advanced programming knowledge of liquid handler platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Labcyte, Agilent), including creating, modifying, and troubleshooting robotics and automation scripts.

  • Strong understanding of the science underpinning laboratory workflows and assays, and how equipment capabilities and limitations affect automation design and data quality.

  • Strong communication skills and demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

  • Demonstrated track record of taking initiative and driving durable improvements to systems, workflows, or team practices.

Desirable

  • Track record of delivering automation solutions in a biologics discovery setting and influencing scientific direction and technical strategy in automation-related projects.

  • Experience implementing automation with orchestration platforms (e.g., Green Button Go, Thermo Momentum, Cellario).

  • Working knowledge of Python, C#, or similar languages, practical experience in database connectivity, data management, and extracting data from ASCII/delimited files to enable automation-related informatics integration and data-driven science.

  • Contributions to technology innovation through conference presentations, publications, patents, or external vendor/partner collaborations.

description:

The WIDS Specialist Level III is responsible for administering the Bastille WIDS platform, leading Monitoring & Response (M&R) activities, analyzing wireless threats, and ensuring compliance with DoD and IC requirements. As such, the WIDS Specialist Level III will need a strong understanding of the Bastille WIDS system, DoD/IC wireless protocols, RF theory, and comprehensive knowledge of National and DoD directives, orders, regulations, and instructions governing the conduct of WIDS activities. Because each WIDS Specialist Level III will have a team of direct reports, experience managing geographically separated teams is expected.

  • Lead M&R activities to identify, investigate, and respond to wireless threats.

  • Utilize wireless monitoring and direction-finding equipment to identify, locate, and report unauthorized devices.

  • Develop and maintain WIDS operating procedures, reporting templates, and technical documentation.

  • Coordinate with Government stakeholders and engineering teams to resolve wireless security incidents.

  • Supervise and mentor WIDS personnel, including geographically dispersed teams.

  • Ensure WIDS operations comply with applicable DoD and IC policies and procedures.

  • Support system deployments, operational readiness, and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Experience conducting M&R activities and wireless incident analysis.

  • Knowledge of DoD and IC policies governing WIDS operations.

  • Experience leading technical teams and coordinating geographically dispersed personnel.

  • Strong written, verbal, and analytical communication skills.

  • Ability to travel worldwide.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Technical Lead to join our client's team and lead the technical delivery of complex technology projects for enterprise clients.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role for someone who can operate at both the technical and strategic level—driving architecture and engineering decisions while working closely with clients, stakeholders, and multidisciplinary teams.
The ideal candidate comes from a technology consulting or professional services environment and has experience leading complex technology initiatives from discovery and solution design through implementation and delivery.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical direction and delivery of complex client engagements.
  • Define and oversee software architecture, system design, integrations, APIs, and technical solutions.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of experience in technology/software engineering, with significant experience in technical leadership.
  • Previous experience in technology consulting, professional services, systems integration, or enterprise technology environments.
  • Experience at organizations such as EY, Deloitte, PwC, KPMG, Accenture, IBM Consulting, or similar firms is highly valued.
  • Proven experience as a Technical Lead, Lead Engineer, Solution Architect, Technical Architect, Engineering Lead, or similar role.
  • Strong understanding of software architecture, system integration, APIs, cloud technologies, databases, and distributed systems.
  • Experience leading complex enterprise technology projects from architecture through implementation.
  • Strong ability to work directly with clients and senior stakeholders.
  • Experience leading, mentoring, and providing technical direction to engineering teams.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to balance technical excellence with business priorities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Advanced English.

What Makes This Role Different

This role is ideal for someone who wants to go beyond simply writing code and take ownership of technical strategy, architecture, delivery, and client impact.
You’ll have the opportunity to work on complex technology initiatives, influence architectural decisions, mentor technical teams, and act as a trusted technical partner to clients.

The Capital Solutions Group within Global Banking & Markets is looking for an Associate to join the Structured Finance - Structured Credit Solutions ("SCS") team in New York. SCS is a diverse and global business that brings together broad capabilities across financing, underwriting, capital raising, risk management and advisory to provide holistic solutions to our clients. The group works closely with classic investment banking, trading and other product groups to originate and execute structured finance transactions.

The SCS team is a market-leading and differentiated franchise focused on pioneering creative and novel structured solutions for corporate clients across all sectors and regions. Working with the SCS team means the opportunity to be involved with some of the most consequential and strategic financings for major corporates. Recent deals include structured equity joint ventures (including digital infrastructure), Esoteric ABS transactions such as airline loyalty-backed financings and spectrum-backed financings, pre-IPO structured HoldCo financings and cross-border asset-backed LBO financings, among others. We are an entrepreneurial team and regularly adjust our focus based on key themes and trends relevant to our clients. In addition to recently executed transactions, we offer solutions spanning hybrid capital, non-traditional project finance, bespoke future flow financings, tax credit monetization, and special situations financings. Associates will work closely with senior bankers in preparing written and oral presentations, running asset and financing analyses, developing credit information for ratings agencies and investors, reviewing legal and other offering documents, and assisting in the valuation and financing associated with M&A, LBO and asset sale transactions.

Job Summary:

Performs duties primarily in support of analyzing Laboratory quality control and patient specimens as well as quality assurance tasks. Operates, maintains and does basic troubleshooting of Laboratory analyzers that perform testing classified as "waived" and "moderate complexity". Collects blood specimens and interacts with patients of diverse ages, backgrounds, values, beliefs and behavior. Receives, handles and processes a variety of specimens for Laboratory testing. Completes computerized tasks related to patient registration and/or test order entry, specimen collection, receiving and processing. Performs basic post-analytic tasks, including distributing reports, storing and/or retrieving specimens. Provides guidance to phlebotomists and lab assistants to promote optimal workflow and rapid problem resolution. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI
  • Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
  • Two years' relevant clinical laboratory experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified Phlebotomy Technician (CPT) license: Preferred

Essential Functions:

  • Loads quality control and patient specimens onto analyzers for testing; follows procedures to ensure the appropriate functioning of the analyzer to ensure testing accuracy and precision. Completes analyzer start-up sequence and function checks according to standard protocol. Prepares reagents and maintains analyzer on-board reagent stock. Collects blood specimens for a variety of Laboratory tests using age-appropriate techniques; handles/transports Lab specimens and provides post-phlebotomy care to patients. Completes computerized tasks as appropriate for affiliate to ensure complete patient registration and/or test order entry into the lab information system, as well as generation of collection lists and/or labels.
  • Receives specimens for testing; assesses specimens upon receipt according to established criteria to determine acceptability; takes action according to protocol including escalating to licensed or certified personnel for direction. Handles and processes a variety of specimen types to prepare them for analysis; adheres to protocols to maintain specimen integrity at all times.
  • Prepares and/or packages specimens for transport to another Adventist Health or outside reference laboratory and may complete computer steps necessary for processing referred specimens, such as compiling tracking lists. Verbally communicates released/reported results. Routes, distributes and retransmits released/reported results. Stores and retrieves specimens. Operates and/or uses basic pre-analytic lab equipment and waived/moderate complexity analytic lab equipment; escalates according to protocol when equipment is malfunctioning.
  • Performs preventive maintenance and minor troubleshooting for Laboratory analyzers. Monitors temperatures and other indicators of environmental and equipment functionality. Maintains an adequate inventory of supplies in work area and/or on phlebotomy cart Participates in managing the laboratory workflow by performing duties such as monitoring pending work, escalating priority work, locating specimens, and coordinating specimen recollections. Maintains required records by completing basic documentation of pre-, post- and analytic work, as well as quality-related tasks.
  • Provides guidance to Lab Assistants to promote optimal workflow and rapid problem resolution. Receives incoming calls for the laboratory and assists the caller as appropriate or transfers these calls to the appropriate laboratory section or person. Communicates with customer to clarify ambiguous, unclear or duplicate test orders Answers patients’ questions within scope of job; appropriately escalates questions that can’t be answered.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

title: Lead Principal Technical Program Manager
description:
OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure) Region Build Organization is currently in need of a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to join our fast-growing team. Technical Program Managers (TPM) rely on their mastery of data and business to understand and anticipate business requirements, initiate programs, track progress, and manage any issues that arise during and after the program completion. As an ideal candidate you possess sufficient technical expertise to communicate business requirements in technical vernacular to engineers and help resolve business blockers.

Additionally, TPMs track technical issues, effectively communicate project status, recommend changes, decide tradeoffs for competing priorities, demonstrate ‘deliver now and iterate’ and deep understanding on the Cloud physical infrastructure (including Datacenter, networking and circuits). They define strategies, regularly participate in executive meetings to present their progress, and share project information with stakeholders. A successful candidate will be well versed in what it takes to drive business growth through data for a cloud organization.

  • 10+ years of experience leading complex technical or engineering programs.

title: Manufacturing Project Engineer
description:

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

This Manufacturing Project Engineer role serves as a global manufacturing engineering leader for Rigid Frame Truck (RFT) Heavy Structures and is embedded within the Product Engineering organization to ensure manufacturability is integrated into the design process from concept through production. In this role, you will lead the development, deployment, and sustainment of common manufacturing processes across the company's global manufacturing footprint, with responsibility spanning structural fabrication, welding, machining, assembly, and inspection. You will collaborate with Product Engineering, regional manufacturing teams, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and automation specialists to standardize methods, equipment strategies, tooling concepts, quality systems, and operational best practices. Your work will improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and capacity performance while enabling repeatable, scalable manufacturing solutions across RFT facilities worldwide.

Additional Information:

  • Primary Location: Decatur, IL.

  • Relocation Assistance: Domestic relocation assistance is available.

  • Travel Requirements: Up to 20% travel (domestic and/or international) may be required.

  • Sponsorship: Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Why This Role Is Impactful:

  • Manufacturing Engineering Leadership Within Product Development – You will serve as the manufacturing engineering expert within the engineering organization, influencing product designs, recommending design changes, and ensuring manufacturing requirements are incorporated early in the development cycle.

  • Global Process Commonality Leadership – You will establish and drive common manufacturing processes and standards across RFT facilities worldwide, reducing variation and enabling consistent, efficient execution.

  • Structural Fabrication and Welding Excellence – You will define and standardize critical manufacturing methods for large-welded structures, including weld procedures, robotic applications, fixtures, tooling, consumables, distortion control, and inspection requirements.

  • Manufacturing Technology and Automation – You will evaluate, develop, and deploy scalable technologies such as robotic welding, automated material handling, dimensional verification systems, offline programming, manufacturing execution systems, and digital work instructions.

  • Operational Performance Improvement – You will leverage Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence principles, KPI dashboards, and data analytics to improve throughput, productivity, capacity utilization, quality, and overall manufacturing cost.

  • Cross-Functional Global Influence – You will lead collaboration among Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and automation teams to develop common solutions that improve manufacturability, standardize processes, and support enterprise manufacturing strategies.

What You Will Do:

  • Lead the development and execution of a global manufacturing process commonality strategy for RFT Heavy Structures, establishing standardized methods, best practices, and scalable manufacturing solutions across global facilities.

  • Serve as the manufacturing engineering representative within the Product Engineering organization, advising design engineers on manufacturability, recommending DFM driven design improvements, and helping drive more efficient and standardized products and processes.

  • Drive global process standardization for fabrication, welding, machining, assembly, material handling, dimensional inspection, and process control to improve quality, efficiency, operational consistency, and manufacturing readiness.

  • Lead capital investment and manufacturing improvement projects, managing scope, budgets, schedules, risks, and stakeholder alignment while delivering measurable business and operational results.

  • Develop and optimize manufacturing processes for large welded structural assemblies, including welding technologies, tooling, automation, quality systems, and production readiness activities, while identifying opportunities to commonize processes across products and manufacturing locations.

  • Apply Lean Manufacturing and Operational Excellence principles to identify process variation, eliminate bottlenecks, resolve manufacturing challenges, and implement sustainable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost.

  • Partner with Product Engineering and cross-functional teams throughout the product development lifecycle to support Design for Manufacturability (DFM), APQP activities, process validation, manufacturing readiness, and successful new product introductions.

  • Strengthen the technical capabilities of the global manufacturing engineering organization by facilitating collaboration, sharing best practices, mentoring engineers, and serving as a subject matter expert for structural manufacturing processes and technology roadmaps.

What Skills you will have:

  • Manufacturing Engineering, Structural Fabrication & Automation: Possesses deep expertise in manufacturing engineering for large structural fabrication environments, including welding, machining, assembly, quality systems, CAD-supported design reviews, robotics, automation, process optimization, and New Product Introduction (NPI) readiness.

  • Project Management & Capacity Planning: Leads complex global manufacturing and capital projects while utilizing advanced capacity planning, forecasting, resource management, budgeting, scheduling, and risk mitigation practices to achieve business objectives.

  • Strategic Problem Solving & Continuous Improvement: Applies analytical thinking, technical troubleshooting, and data-driven decision-making to solve complex manufacturing challenges, optimize processes, eliminate waste, and drive sustainable operational improvements.

  • Global Manufacturing Leadership & Collaboration: Builds alignment across engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and operations teams by influencing stakeholders, driving process standardization, mentoring engineers, and sharing best practices across global organizations.

  • Manufacturing Technology & Digital Engineering: Leverages CAD tools, manufacturing data analytics, automation technologies, manufacturing execution systems, and digital manufacturing solutions to improve product manufacturability, production performance, and operational scalability.

Top Candidates will also have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Welding Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification or equivalent welding qualification.

  • Experience with robotic welding, automation technologies, and advanced manufacturing systems.

  • Demonstrated success developing and implementing global manufacturing standards in a multinational organization.

  • Experience leveraging manufacturing data analytics, digital work instructions, manufacturing execution systems, and offline programming solutions to drive operational excellence.

description:
Title:

Financial Management Analyst

Job Summary

KBR is seeking a Financial Management Analyst to support a complex portfolio of international security cooperation and acquisition programs in Huntsville, Alabama. This position serves as a subject matter expert in financial management and provides planning, analysis, justification, presentation, execution, and reporting activities for Foreign Military Sales (FMS), Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative (USAI), Building Partnership Capacity (BPC), Special Defense Acquisition Fund (SDAF), Funded Reimbursable Authority (FRA), and related funding sources. The role supports multiple Department of War acquisition programs and weapon system portfolios, including Javelin, Joint Air-to-Ground Missile (JAGM), TOW, and Hydra systems, representing significant program value and funding execution requirements. Working across all phases of the acquisition lifecycle, the analyst collaborates with program leadership, functional teams, and government stakeholders to ensure effective financial stewardship and mission execution. This position plays a critical role in aligning financial resources with program objectives while supporting strategic decision-making and long-range planning.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Perform short-range and long-range financial planning, programming, budgeting, forecasting, and funding analysis for assigned acquisition programs.
  • Analyze, monitor, and execute FMS, USAI, BPC, SDAF, FRA, and other appropriated funding sources in support of program objectives.
  • Develop financial reports, briefings, budget exhibits, and executive-level presentations for government and program leadership.
  • Track obligations, expenditures, commitments, and execution metrics across a large portfolio of weapon system programs and cases.
  • Conduct financial reviews and reconcile funding data to ensure accuracy, compliance, and audit readiness.
  • Support budget formulation activities, funding requests, reprogramming actions, and resource allocation decisions.
  • Provide financial guidance to program managers and functional stakeholders regarding funding availability, execution status, and fiscal constraints.
  • Assess financial impacts of program changes, emerging requirements, and acquisition milestones throughout the program lifecycle.
  • Coordinate with contracting, logistics, engineering, and acquisition teams to align financial resources with mission requirements.
  • Other duties as assigned in support of mission and business requirements.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or related field.
  • Active Secret Clearance OR the ability to obtain and maintain.
  • 2+ years of experience in financial management, budgeting, accounting, financial analysis, or program financial support.
  • Experience supporting government-funded programs, contracts, or acquisition efforts.
  • Experience preparing financial reports, budget documentation, and funding analyses.
  • Experience utilizing Microsoft Excel and other financial management tools for data analysis and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs.
  • Experience with USAI, BPC, SDAF, FRA, or other security assistance funding sources.
  • Experience supporting Department of War acquisition programs or ACAT I weapon system programs.
  • Knowledge of Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) processes.
  • Experience supporting missile, munitions, or defense weapon system portfolios

title: Sr. Scientist II - Toxicology - Onsite in Aliso Viejo, CA
description:
The Sr. Scientist II, Toxicology is responsible for leading and executing nonclinical toxicology programs supporting the development of novel drug delivery devices and combination products. This role provides advanced scientific expertise in the design, monitoring, interpretation, and reporting of toxicology and safety studies that enable clinical development and regulatory submissions. The position independently manages complex projects, collaborates extensively with multidisciplinary teams, and contributes to the development of nonclinical strategies aligned with program objectives. The Sr. Scientist II serves as a key scientific resource within Toxicology and influences decision-making through technical expertise, data interpretation, and risk assessment.

Sr. Scientist II, Toxicology

How You’ll Contribute:

The Sr. Scientist II, Toxicology is responsible for leading and executing nonclinical toxicology programs supporting the development of novel drug delivery devices and combination products. This role provides advanced scientific expertise in the design, monitoring, interpretation, and reporting of toxicology and safety studies that enable clinical development and regulatory submissions. The position independently manages complex projects, collaborates extensively with multidisciplinary teams, and contributes to the development of nonclinical strategies aligned with program objectives. The Sr. Scientist II serves as a key scientific resource within Toxicology and influences decision-making through technical expertise, data interpretation, and risk assessment.

What You’ll Do:

Nonclinical Development & Study Leadership

  • Leads the design, execution, monitoring, and reporting of nonclinical toxicology and safety studies supporting pharmaceuticals, drug delivery devices and combination products.
  • Develops and implements nonclinical study strategies to support IND, IMPD, NDA, BLA and MAA submissions and clinical development programs.
  • Evaluates published and unpublished data to assess safety risks associated with new ingredients, materials, formulations, and delivery technologies.
  • Serves as Study Monitor for GLP and non-GLP studies, ensuring scientific quality, regulatory compliance, and alignment with development objectives.
  • Designs scientifically robust studies that maximize data quality while promoting ethical animal use and regulatory compliance.
  • Coordinates study timelines, priorities, and deliverables across multiple programs to support development milestones.
  • Manages CRO relationships, including vendor selection, protocol development, bid evaluation, study oversight, and review of final reports.

Data Interpretation & Regulatory Support

  • Reviews, analyzes, and interprets nonclinical study data to generate scientifically sound conclusions and recommendations.
  • Contributes to the preparation and review of toxicology sections for regulatory submissions, investigator brochures, and internal development documents.
  • Identifies potential safety risks and develops mitigation strategies through integration of data from multiple disciplines and study types.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Technical Leadership

  • Serves as the toxicology representative on cross-functional project teams and provides scientific input to development plans and program decisions.

Collaborates closely with Chemistry, Engineering, Pharmacology, Pharmacokinetics, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Development, and external partners

  • Participates in regulatory interactions and supports responses to questions from global health authorities.
  • Evaluates competitor products, emerging technologies, and scientific literature to inform program strategy and innovation opportunities.
  • Provides mentorship and technical guidance to junior scientists and project team members as appropriate.

How You’ll Get There:

  • Demonstrated expertise in GLP toxicology studies, laboratory animal sciences, FDA regulations, ICH guidelines, and nonclinical safety assessment.
  • Proven ability to independently lead complex technical projects and exercise sound scientific judgment in study design and data interpretation.
  • Experience managing external CROs and coordinating cross-functional development activities.
  • Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate complex scientific concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Demonstrated success contributing to regulatory submissions and supporting nonclinical development strategies.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Toxicology, Biological Sciences, or related scientific discipline with 12+ years of relevant experience.
  • Master's Degree in Toxicology, Biological Sciences, or related scientific discipline with 10+ years of relevant experience.
  • PhD in Toxicology, Biological Sciences, or related scientific discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience.
  • DABT certification preferred
  • Willingness to travel around 15%
  • This role works onsite in Aliso Viejo, CA
  • Relocation assistance may be available

DEPARTMENT: In-Room Dining

JOB TITLE: In-Room Dining Server

REPORTS TO: In-Room Dining Manager/Shift Supervisor

SUPERVISES: n/a

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF POSITION:

Delivers food and beverage orders to guest rooms according to hotel specifications, courteously and efficiently. Also assists in the maintenance of the In-Room Dining area and equipment.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND JOB DUTIES:

  • Maintain complete knowledge of all liquor brands, beers and non-alcoholic selections available in In-Room Dining.
  • Maintain knowledge of the particular characteristics and description of every wine/champagne by the glass and major wines on the wine list.
  • Maintain complete knowledge of designated glassware and garnishes for drinks.
  • Maintain complete knowledge of all menu items, preparation method, ingredients, sauces, preparation time, garnishes, presentation and prices.
  • Maintain complete knowledge of guest room layout, locations and room numbers/names.
  • Maintain complete knowledge and strictly abide by state liquor regulations, particularly those prohibiting service to minors, intoxicated persons and drunk driving.
  • Maintain complete knowledge of correct maintenance and use of equipment, use equipment only as intended.
  • Maintain complete knowledge and comply with all departmental policies/service procedures.
  • Maintain knowledge of Micros and manual systems.
  • Answer In-Room Dining phone within 3 rings, using correct salutations and telephone etiquette.
  • Complete opening side duties as assigned:
    • Check quality and amount of all In-Room Dining stock and supplies using checklist.
    • Fold/stack In-Room Dining napkins.
    • Requisition all necessary supplies and transport from storeroom to In-Room Dining.
    • Set tables and trays according to service standards.
    • Set up all condiments (butter, jellies, syrups, juices) and beverages (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) according to service standards.
    • Ensure a sufficient supply of all silverware, glassware and chinaware for service.
    • Prepare all cold food items (cereals, fruits, salads).
    • Check cleanliness and condition of all equipment for use in In-Room Dining area, rectify any deficiencies.
    • Ensure all flowers and decorative items are fresh for guest use.
  • Retrieve all food orders from kitchen and place on table/tray in accordance with the departmental standards.
  • Retrieve all alcoholic beverage items from bar and place on table/tray in accordance with the departmental standards.
  • Transport tables/trays from In-Room Dining area to guest rooms, ensuring all standards of food presentation are maintained and that no spillage occurs.
  • Enter the guest room and place the table/tray by following the established departmental procedures.
  • Serve the food items and beverages to the guest in accordance with departmental standards.
  • Open and serve wine/champagne bottles.
  • Anticipate guests' needs, respond promptly and acknowledge all guests even when busy.
  • Maintain positive guest relations.
  • Be familiar with all hotel services/features and local attractions/activities to respond to guest inquiries accurately.
  • Handle guest complaints following the instant pacification procedures and ensuring guest satisfaction.
  • Present check to guest for signature/payment. Adhere to all payment procedures established by Finance.
  • Set up and deliver amenities to designated rooms.
  • Monitor and maintain cleanliness, sanitation and organization of all service areas, guest rooms and guest corridors following procedures laid down in departmental standards.
  • Transport all tables/trays from guest rooms to In-Room Dining area as assigned.
  • Clean and reset tables/trays, maintaining sufficient supply in the In-Room Dining area.
  • Collect and report tips at the end of the assigned shift.
  • Complete closing side duties:
    • Properly store all reusable goods.
    • Breakdown all goods as specified in departmental standards.
    • Retrieve tables/trays from guest rooms and breakdown accordingly.
    • Clean all equipment as assigned in the side duties.
    • Restock items for next service.
    • Remove all dirty linen; fold napkins.
    • Marry and stock all condiments.
    • Reset tables/trays.
  • Complete all closing reports as assigned.
  • AM - Set up and deliver doorknob orders.
  • PM - Collect doorknob menus from guest rooms.
  • Successful completion of the training/certification process.
  • Relieve Order Taker/Cashier as assigned:
    • Take guest orders and record such as specified in departmental service procedures.
    • Utilize suggestive/ up selling techniques when taking orders.
    • Input order into system and ensure transmission of food orders is verified by kitchen.
    • Legibly document orders when system is down and distribute food orders to kitchen.
    • Process payment of guest checks according to Accounting procedures.
  • Obtain cigars/cigarettes when requested by guests.
  • Follow maintenance program and cleaning schedule.
  • Replace flowers in bud vases.
  • Polish silver trays and coffee pots.
  • Expedite on floor or in kitchen as assigned.
  • Complete office paperwork (filing).
  • Legibly document pertinent information in In-Room Dining logbook.

  • Legibly document maintenance needs on work orders and submit to manager.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Ability to exert physical effort in transporting trays and tables from service area to guests.
  • Ability to endure abundant physical movements throughout the work areas.

SPECIAL SKILLS REQUIRED:

  • Ability to understand guests' service needs.
  • Ability to be well organized, maintain concentration and think clearly when providing service to guest rooms within any given period of time.
  • Ability to focus on details.
  • Ability to maintain good coordination while serving orders quickly.
  • Ability to perform job functions with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to work cohesively with co-workers as part of a team.

EDUCATION REQUIRED:

High school graduate, some college.

EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

  • Two year‘s experience as a In-Room Dining Server.
  • Experience in In-Room Dining order taking is preferred.

LICENSES OR CERTIFICATES:

  • Food handling certificate.
  • Certification of previous training in liquor, wine and food service is preferred.
  • Certification in C.P.R is preferred.
  • Certification in alcohol awareness program is preferred.

$19.06 +tips

The Hospice Chaplain is responsible for the provision of spiritual care services to patients and families/caregivers of Symbii Home Health & Hospice, SLC, either directly or through coordination of care with other spiritual counselors.

Assures spiritual assessment of patients and families/caregivers in the hospice program and appropriate services are rendered in a timely manner.

Assists in supervision of spiritual care volunteers when assigned to patients/ families/caregivers.

Actively participates in quality assessment performance improvement teams and activities.

Accepts and performs other related duties and responsibilities as required.

Graduate of accredited seminary or school of theology (BD, MDiv or equivalent theological degree). Experience working with death and dying, individuals/family/caregiver.

Ability to work as member of interdisciplinary group.

Comfortable in an interfaith setting.

Ability to accept different lifestyles, cultures, beliefs, and values.

Ability to network with community clergy and congregations.

Knowledge of and commitment to hospice philosophy of care.

Hospice/experience preferred.

In this highly collaborative role, you will lead and influence validation strategies and testing activities, working closely with teams at Tucson Proving Grounds (TPG), global engineering partners, and customers around the world.   • Share best practices with the design teams, using tools such as Machine Readiness Summary (MRS) and presentations from the best practitioners.

  • As validation needs become known for which there is no robust validation method, the validation engineer will collaborate with teams to assess the risk and develop a plan.

  • Determine new engineering content percentage for NPI programs.

  • Prepare and present Machine Readiness Summary and Risk Assessment for NPI programs.

Knowledge of validation methodologies, risk assessment tools, and engineering processes used to evaluate product performance and ensure design requirements are met.

Analytical Thinking: Strong ability to analyze test results, identify failure modes, assess technical risks, and develop data-driven solutions to improve product performance, reliability, and serviceability. Skilled at making sound engineering decisions in complex and evolving situations.

Effective Communications: Ability to communicate technical information clearly and effectively to engineers, product groups, validation teams, customers, and leadership. Experience presenting validation status, risk assessments, and recommendations while fostering collaboration across global and cross-functional teams.

Product Design and Development: Understanding of new product development and continuous product improvement processes, including validation planning, product readiness assessments, and design reviews. Experience supporting product development activities by ensuring validation requirements are aligned with performance, durability, and quality objectives.

Bachelor’s degree in an accredited Engineering curriculum.

Knowledge of Caterpillar processes (i.e., NPI, NTI, CPI, etc.).

Strong analytical skills and mechanical aptitude.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Experience working in a global engineering environment.

Ability to multitask and adjust to changing priorities as needs arise.

Prior off-highway machine design experience.

title: Executive Support Senior Program Manager, Tech Advisor
location: Boston, MA; Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY; Washington, DC
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

We're looking for a technology program manager to own the technical needs that follow our executives outside the four walls of the enterprise: their homes, their vehicles, and their travel. Reporting to the Protective Services Lead, this role sits at the intersection of physical security technology, hands-on program delivery, and vendor management. The Engineering & Technology Lead sets the architecture and strategic plan for security technology across GSIS; you'll own execution for the personal and residential slice of that footprint, the systems that protect executives and their families wherever they actually are, not just at the office.

This is not a coordination-only role. You'll need enough technical fluency to make good calls on the ground without waiting for architecture sign-off on every decision, enough program rigor to keep vendors and installs on track, and enough judgment to know when something belongs back with the Protective Services Lead because it touches strategy or standards beyond your scope. Much of the documentation you produce will be read by people who never see the systems themselves, so clarity matters as much as technical correctness.

Responsibilities

  • Own residential security system design, integration, and lifecycle management for assigned executive residences (cameras, alarms, access control, sensor networks), aligned to the standards set by the Protective Services Lead
  • Own home network design and hardening for executive residences and travel, coordinating with corporate IT/InfoSec standards where they intersect
  • Manage the technology side of travel security: secure communications provisioning, single-use travel hardware, and rapid-deployment kits for new or temporary properties
  • Manage the vendor relationships and contracts for the residential and personal technology stack, installers, monitoring providers, communications providers, within the governance framework the Protective Service Lead sets
  • Maintain system health monitoring, managed maintenance, and as-built documentation for technology deployed outside the enterprise perimeter
  • Own decommissioning and transition of technology when properties or vehicles change, so nothing orphaned (access, data, or hardware) gets left behind
  • Act as first point of contact and triage for executive and family requests involving personal technology and security systems, resolving directly where you can and routing to the Protective Services Lead when it requires a broader architecture or strategy decision
  • Contribute audit-ready documentation for the technology under your ownership to support regulatory, customer, and partner diligence requests

You may be a good fit if you

  • Bring hands-on physical security technology experience from residential, travel, or personal-protection contexts, not only corporate/enterprise systems
  • Have solid program management experience delivering security technology, you know what a well-run install, vendor relationship, or rapid deployment actually looks like
  • Have contributed to or led the build of security technology capabilities from zero in a high-growth environment, including documentation, playbooks, and training
  • Can manage vendor relationships through a full lifecycle: selection, contracting, onboarding, performance management, and renewal
  • Write clearly and can translate technical tradeoffs for audiences that range from engineers to principals to household staff
  • Are comfortable operating with moderate ambiguity, and know when a decision is yours to make versus one that belongs with whoever owns the broader technology strategy
  • Care about Anthropic's mission and the unique security considerations that come with building frontier AI systems

Strong candidates may also:

  • Have 10+ years of experience delivering physical security technology programs
  • Have direct experience with residential or executive-protection-adjacent technology deployments specifically, not just corporate office systems
  • Have worked at an AI-focused organization, frontier technology company, or similarly high-growth, high-scrutiny environment
  • Have managed distributed vendor networks across multiple properties or regions

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Raytheon's Receiver/Exciter & Processing Architecture (REPA) Department is the focal point for receiver, exciter, beam steering, and signal processing technology within Raytheon. The department is responsible for the design, development, integration, and support to production builds, and lifecycle support of Raytheon products.

We have an opportunity for a Senior Principal RF Design Engineer who is seeking to utilize their academic background and professional experience in RF / Microwave system theory and design to help develop the next generation of Raytheon’s Radar Receiver, Exciter, and Transmitter products.

  • Architecture development, requirements analysis, hardware design, hands-on testing of components, circuit card assemblies, and subsystems.

  • Design and development of transmitters, receivers, or exciters.

  • Design and optimization of RF circuits – either chains of components (receiver, exciter, etc.) or individual parts (filters, limiters, couplers, etc.).

  • Working with interdisciplinary teams – power, digital, mechanical, etc.

  • Schematic capture and RF routing.

  • Technical support during the transition to production and support to production activities.

  • Cost and schedule management plus proposal writing.

  • This 1st shift position will be 100% on-site & based in either Tewksbury, MA or Marlborough, MA, with travel between multiple MA sites anticipated.

Qualifications You Must Have:

  • Typically requires a degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) and a minimum of 10 years’ of prior relevant experience.

  • Experience with Microwave/RF system, subsystem and/or component analysis, design and/or test.

  • Experience with electromagnetic simulation tools (e.g., HFSS, ADS, CST, and/or Mentor Graphics’ Xpedition) and analytical tools (e.g., MATLAB).

  • The ability to obtain and maintain an Interim Secret U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

  • Experience working in design, from concept through production.

  • Experience translating system performance and operation specifications into hardware requirements, design, and test specifications.

  • Background in designing for manufacturability, producibility, and cost constraints, which includes yield and margin analysis.

  • Problem-solving skills with ability to proactively identify alternate solutions to overcome difficult technical challenges.

  • Experience in technical writing and oral presentations.

  • Technical background in any of the following areas:

    • Cascade analysis and/or frequency planning

    • Filter design and fabrication

    • Circuit card assembly and fabrication

    • High speed data converter test / characterization

    • Low Noise RF source design and test experience

title: Software Engineer III - Mobile
description:
We have an exciting and rewarding opportunity for you to take your software engineering career to the next level.

As a Software Engineer III at JPMorgan Chase within the Consumer & Community Banking, you serve as a seasoned member of an agile team to design and deliver trusted market-leading technology products in a secure, stable, and scalable way. You are responsible for carrying out critical technology solutions across multiple technical areas within various business functions in support of the firm’s business objectives.

Job responsibilities

  • Designs and delivers iOS software solutions by translating product requirements into scalable mobile architectures (e.g., MVC/MVVM/Clean), implementing features in Swift (UIKit/SwiftUI), and applying non-routine thinking to build elegant solutions and rapidly decompose complex technical issues through root-cause analysis, instrumentation, and debugging (Xcode, Instruments, crash logs).
  • Builds secure, production-grade iOS code by writing high-quality, maintainable components and performance-conscious algorithms that integrate reliably with backend services and device capabilities, leveraging modern iOS concurrency patterns (GCD/Combine/async/await) to coordinate synchronous/asynchronous workflows, and enforcing mobile security best practices (secure storage/Keychain, data protection, least-privilege permissions, input validation).
  • Produces iOS architecture and design artifacts for complex mobile applications by documenting end-to-end designs (module boundaries, data flow, navigation, state management, offline/online sync, API contracts) and maintaining accountability that design constraints (performance, accessibility, security, resilience, battery/network efficiency) are implemented and enforced in Swift code through reviews, standards, and automated checks.
  • Gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes mobile and platform telemetry from large, diverse datasets (crash reports, performance traces, app analytics, network logs, CI/CD signals, feature-flag metrics, customer feedback) and develops clear visualizations/reporting (dashboards, release health summaries, regression trackers) to drive continuous improvement of iOS app quality and system reliability.
  • Proactively uncovers hidden issues and patterns in iOS codebases and operational data (recurring crash signatures, memory leaks, ANRs/hangs, excessive network chatter, slow renders, flaky tests, dependency risk) and uses these insights to improve coding hygiene (refactoring, modularization, test coverage, linting, documentation) and evolve the app/system architecture (better layering, concurrency model, caching strategy, observability).
  • Leverages enterprise-authorized AI coding assist tools within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and productivity across complex deliverables (e.g., code generation/refactoring, unit test creation, documentation), while validating outputs through peer review, automated testing, and secure coding standards; contributes learnings and reusable patterns to improve broader team effectiveness.
  • Applies knowledge of tools within the Software Development Life Cycle toolchain, including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development and automation capabilities, to improve the value realized by automation.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and 3+ years applied experience
  • Hands-on experience designing iOS/mobile systems end-to-end, including application development in Swift (UIKit/SwiftUI), unit/UI testing (XCTest/XCUITest), and ensuring operational stability through monitoring, crash triage, performance tuning, and production support processes.
  • Proven ability to develop, debug, and maintain code in a large enterprise environment using modern languages (Swift) and data/querying technologies relevant to mobile workflows (e.g., SQL fundamentals, REST/GraphQL usage and troubleshooting, log/metric querying via observability tools).
  • Strong working knowledge of the Software Development Life Cycle (requirements → design → implementation → testing → release → monitoring/incident response), with an emphasis on mobile release management (App Store/TestFlight, phased rollouts, feature flags).
  • Solid understanding of Agile delivery practices, including CI/CD for iOS (build pipelines, automated tests, code quality gates), application resiliency (graceful degradation, offline support, retries/backoff, crash-free sessions), and mobile security (secure storage/Keychain, encryption in transit/at rest where applicable, OWASP MASVS concepts, privacy and permission handling).
  • Hands-on experience using enterprise-authorized AI-assisted software development tools within the work environment (e.g., for coding, test creation, troubleshooting, or documentation) with demonstrated ability to critically evaluate, validate, and refine AI-generated outputs for correctness, performance, and security.
  • Understanding of responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data sensitivity considerations, secure handling of inputs/outputs, and adherence to resiliency and security expectations; ability to guide peers on safe and effective usage within team practices.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Familiarity with modern front-end technologies and patterns that commonly interface with mobile clients (e.g., component-based UI concepts, TypeScript/React basics, webviews, design systems) and the ability to collaborate effectively with web and design teams.
  • Exposure to cloud technologies used by mobile ecosystems, such as API gateways, authentication/identity (OAuth2/OIDC), serverless/event-driven backends, storage/CDNs, and mobile observability/analytics platforms; comfortable diagnosing issues across client–backend boundaries.
  • Familiarity with Objective-C a plus

Key responsibilities include reducing process or handling defects throughout inbound to outbound processes, ensuring operational quality and data accuracy, and developing and implementing loss/incident prevention strategies. Additionally, optimizing the Andon Cord process, leading Kaizen projects for continuous improvement, and managing a team of on-site ICQA operation members are crucial to this role. This position offers a valuable opportunity to drive significant improvements in our inventory and quality assurance processes.

  • ICQA Personnel Performance Management:

    • Manage the performance of on-site Inventory Control and Quality Assurance (ICQA) personnel.

  • Project Management:

    • Initiate Kaizen projects and drive continuous improvement and optimization.

    • Participate in team projects as requested.

  • BS in Industrial Engineering, Operations Engineering, Process Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related discipline.

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in inventory management, with a preference for those with Inventory Control experience.

  • Attention to detail with an emphasis on data and operational precision, adept at identifying and implementing systems to minimize discrepancies or errors.

  • Data-Driven mindset with a focus on achieving measurable outcomes.

  • Expertise in Lean Management principles and familiarity with methodologies such as 5S, root cause analysis and Kaizen.

  • Demonstrated ability to foster continuous improvement and operational excellence through innovative solutions.

  • Proficiency in data analysis using SQL, Excel, and other standard development tools.

  • Onsite requirements- Edison NJ 08817

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills in both English and Mandarin

title: Survey/Geomatics Technologist
description:
About Us
Aplin Martin is a full-service Civil Engineering, Architecture, Planning, Environmental and Survey company, celebrating over 57 years of success in making sustainable communities a reality across Canada. Over the five decades, the Aplin Martin family has grown into a multi-disciplinary firm of around 300 talented and dedicated professionals delivering innovative and practical design solutions, approval strategies, and project management services to our clients in BC, AB, and ON. We are dedicated to nurturing our employees’ growth and development and providing a supportive environment with a strong emphasis on mentorship and professional development that ensures a rewarding career within our organization.

Position Overview:
The Geomatics Technologist will work on a wide range of projects from land development and strata/air space work, topographic and rights-of-way surveys, surveys for infrastructure and capital works projects, construction and monitoring surveys, surveys on First Nation lands and many other diverse types of surveys. The Geomatics Technologist will work primarily in the field under the direction of a Project Manager leading the Survey process on sites and supervise the Survey Assistant.


Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work closely with Project Manager/Land Surveyor to ensure survey procedures are followed and project expectations are met.
  • Perform various types of surveys that may include legal, topographic, right of ways, construction layout, as built and engineering surveys.
  • Collect data in the field using a variety of tools including data collectors, robotic total stations and GNSS receivers.
  • Prepare clear and accurate field notes and sketches.
  • Ensure collected data is accurate and standard survey procedures have been followed.
  • Maintain survey vehicle and equipment.
  • Work with clients in a professional manner.
  • Perform survey computations in the field.
  • Assist in training and developing new team members.
  • Follow all safety guidelines provided by Aplin & Martin.
  • Complete Field Level Hazard Assessment on a daily basis.
  • Assist the Project Manager with organizing and scheduling for the following days’ field work and coordinating with the Survey Assistant.
  • Clear vegetation and debris in order for measurements to be taken.
  • Upload and download survey data on a daily basis; and,
  • Any other duties as assigned.


Skills and Qualifications:

  • Survey Technology Diploma and at least 5, preferably more than 10 years’ experience in survey setting, preferably in Lower Mainland.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with field crews, project managers, clients, and other project stakeholders.
  • Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills, with a high level of dependability, initiative, and attention to detail.
  • Strong working knowledge of robotic total stations, conventional survey technologies, and GNSS solutions.
  • Must have demonstrated experience with high-precision monitoring and construction layout, including the ability to work to tight survey tolerances and accurately interpret and apply engineering and construction drawings in the field.
  • Ability to interpret legal survey plans and legal survey evidence
  • Proficient with Leica survey equipment and software, including Captivate and Leica Infinity/GeoCloud
  • A Transport Canada Advanced RPAS (UAV) Pilot Certificate is considered an asset.
  • Experience operating Uncrewed Surface Vessels (USVs) and sonar/bathymetric survey equipment is considered an asset.
  • Experience operating terrestrial laser scanning equipment, such as the Leica RTC360, is considered an asset.
  • Ability to work independently and take initiative while also working effectively as part of a survey team.
  • Willingness to undertake occasional overnight and out-of-town work, with the majority of work occurring within the region.
  • Ability to work in a variety of outdoor settings and weather conditions.
  • Physically fit and capable of lifting and carrying survey equipment.
  • A valid BC driver’s license, with excellent driving record. A driver abstract will be required.

The hourly range for this position is $38 to 48 per hour, commensurate with experience, skillsets, and qualifications.

Position Overview:
The Non-QM Income Scenario Specialist (Wholesale) is responsible for providing income calculations and reviews for loans prior to underwriter review. The Non-QM Income Scenario Specialist takes initiative and works with others to meet turn times and maintains customer satisfaction, while providing accurate income calculations for all specified loan types and products. This position interprets investor guidelines and applies them to the method being used to calculate income for specified investor(s). The Non-QM Income Scenario Specialist articulates these guidelines and provides explanation of the calculations and methods to all applicable parties.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Perform daily loan support for company employees via a ticketing system, inbound phone calls, email, and in person for underwriting/loan scenario-based questions and communication.

  • Review and respond to general income calculation and documentation questions while maintaining thorough knowledge of investor income guidelines.

  • Assist Loan Officers and Loan Processors in calculating income per investor guidelines and specifications; types of income to be calculated will be from sources including, but not limited to, self-employment, asset depletion, bank statement qualification, debt-service-ratios, wage earners, other income sources (capital gains, rental income, etc.).

  • Analyze various underwriting scenarios and suggest potential alternate options with different investors, as needed.

  • Review, analyze, and calculate income using complex income documentation, including personal and business tax returns, bank statements, audited/unaudited profit and loss statements, balance sheets, rental income documentation, etc. and provide calculations to be used for qualifying purposes.

  • Analyze and calculate income and determine business liquidity per investor guidelines.

  • Maintain knowledge of IRS income filing forms as they pertain to underwriting qualification, including but not limited to 1040’s, 1120-S, 1065, 1120, as well as all applicable forms, schedules, and statements within these documents.

  • Create technical documentation, system documentation, “how to” guides, FAQs, and self-help references as needed.

  • Track tasks, activities, and time spent within the ticketing system and meet expected turn-times.

  • Participate in Underwriting Department, Regional, and Sales calls, lead calls as necessary.

  • Collaborate amongst team members and other departments.

  • Maintain a working knowledge of essential underwriting information.

  • Maintain all Underwriting designations, as applicable.

  • Promote risk-awareness, ensure efficient and effective risk and compliance management practices by adhering to required standards and processes.

  • Ensure compliance with anti-money laundering and sanctions laws and regulations.

Qualifications and Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience, preferred.

  • Minimum 4 years of underwriting experience, underwriting to multiple agency and investor guidelines, preferred.

  • Jumbo/Non-Agency and Non-QM underwriting background, preferred.

  • Experience using LoanBeam and Encompass, preferred.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, customer service, and problem-solving skills.

  • Proficient with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

The Mechanical Analysis and Test (MA&T) Department is responsible for ensuring structural and thermal design robustness across the Raytheon portfolio of products. From preliminary concepts to fielded weapon system support, MA&T delivers innovative structural and thermal engineering solutions utilizing methods ranging from classical fundamental & empirically based techniques to state-of-the-art finite element methods leveraging industry leading commercial tools; all complimented and validated by tests executed in a manner to ensure cost effective yet technically balanced solutions.

The Thermal Analyst II position is located in Huntsville, AL and the role is onsite.

As an early career Thermal Analyst, you will be responsible for detailed thermal analysis on products throughout their lifecycle from initial design trade studies and proposals through qualification testing to enduring production support. The analysis will cover a wide range of difficult problems, requiring solutions that are imaginative, thorough, practicable, and consistent with organization objectives. The analysis tasks will span the spectrum from classical hand analyses to detailed analyses requiring the use of finite element analysis software. A Thermal Engineer of this salary grade is expected to have a level of technical competence with thermodynamic principles. The Thermal Engineer will be held accountable for completing his/her work within the agreed upon cost and schedule. Additionally, the selected candidate will be expected to present their work for peer reviews and to be a peer reviewer for other engineers’ work. Finally, the engineer is expected to plan and support tests, perform data reduction and engage in thermal model correlation.

  • Perform detailed thermal analyses to solve various program thermal challenges
  • Generate test plans required to validate analyses and verify hardware compliance to customer requirements

  • Experience in mechanical principles to solve classical thermal analysis solutions both inside and outside of finite element tools and an ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities
  • Ability to obtain a U.S. government issued security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance, Clearance must be active and transferable prior to start date
  • Ability to work in a collaborative, team-based environment and independently

  • 5+ years of professional experience in the thermal analysis of complex systems that require collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines
  • Experience with solid modeling CAD tools such as CREO or equivalent
  • Experience in Electronics Cooling and Aerodynamic Heating Analyses
  • Demonstrated experience in thermal testing: Planning, organization, execution, data reduction and correlation
  • Experience presenting to external customers

title: Asset Protection Officer, Bellevue Square - Part Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story.

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Officer, you are a visible and welcoming presence who helps create a safe, secure, and service-focused shopping environment. Stationed at key entrances and high-shortage areas, you help deter theft, identify potential risk, support customer and colleague safety, and partner with store teams to deliver a positive experience for everyone who enters the store.

Why This Role Matters

This entry-level role is more than traditional security — it is presence with purpose. Whether greeting customers, helping deter theft, supporting team safety, or responding calmly during incidents, Asset Protection Officers help customers and colleagues feel comfortable, confident, and cared for while protecting the business.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.
  • On the floor, they focus on the customer - offering a warm welcome, making eye contact, and creating friendly customer experience.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

What To Expect

  • Serve as a visible and reassuring presence at store entrances, high-traffic areas, and high-shortage locations.
  • Help deter theft and identify suspicious activity while maintaining a welcoming, customer-first approach.
  • Partner with store teams and Asset Protection leaders to support safety, service, and shortage reduction.
  • Respond calmly and professionally to incidents, medical situations, and other store needs.
  • Use technology and two-way communication devices to stay connected and support timely response.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Create a safe and welcoming first impression by greeting customers and maintaining a visible presence in key areas of the store.
  • Help protect company assets by deterring theft, identifying suspicious behavior, and supporting shortage reduction efforts.
  • Assist with apprehensions under the direction of Asset Protection Leaders, Captains, or Detectives.
  • Document theft, accidents, audits, and other incidents through accurate and timely reporting.
  • Conduct operational audits and complete assigned Asset Protection tasks as directed.
  • Support a culture of safety and service by partnering with store teams and responding appropriately to customer and colleague needs.
  • Follow company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, evidence handling, and confidential information.
  • Respond to medical situations and help facilitate basic first aid for customers and colleagues.
  • Provide testimony in criminal or civil legal proceedings, as needed.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays, with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality.
