title: Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer, AI Products
description:
Being sick or injured is painful. Getting better shouldn’t be.

Most industries have been transformed by new technology. Healthcare is still waiting — and you can help change that.

Our mission is simple but ambitious: make healthcare accessible, transparent, and effortless for all. We put the consumer at the center, move fast and partner with forward-thinking providers to deliver software that makes care better, faster, and more human. This is work with real-world stakes — and you can help lead the way.

Solv is building AI-powered healthcare infrastructure that makes everyday care easier for patients and the teams who care for them—from finding and receiving care to helping clinics reduce manual work, improve access, and run better operations.

Near-term work will likely include voice and other AI agents supporting scheduling, billing, and additional healthcare workflows. However, this is a broader product-engineering role, and the problems and technologies will evolve.

We’re looking for a senior generalist with strong web fundamentals, product judgment, curiosity, and ownership. You will work closely with a product manager to shape solutions while owning technical decisions, execution, production quality, and results.

You do not need to have worked professionally on an AI-native team, but meaningful hands-on AI work is required. That experience may come from production work, internal tools, prototypes, open source, personal projects, or self-directed experimentation.

You can expect to:

  • Partner with product, design, customers, and engineers to turn business and user problems into shipped improvements.
  • Build across the full stack, including frontend experiences, backend services, APIs, relational data models, integrations, and AI-powered workflows.
  • Take ideas from early exploration through implementation, production rollout, and iteration.
  • Build scrappy prototypes to learn quickly, then develop reliable production systems when an opportunity is proven.
  • Improve AI systems using evaluations, production traces, customer feedback, product data, and operational signals.
  • Design for uncertainty through testing, observability, guardrails, fallbacks, auditability, and human escalation.
  • Build enterprise healthcare products that account for privacy, permissions, edge cases, data quality, reliability, and supportability.
  • Explore new AI capabilities while balancing speed, quality, safety, cost, customer value, and maintainability.

Position Title:

Program Coordinator - Regional Hub (THRIVE)

Job Description Summary:

The Regional Hub Program Coordinator provides operational and administrative support for the Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative within an assigned Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) regional hub. This position coordinates day-to-day implementation activities, training and onboarding logistics, meeting and communication activities, documentation and record management, and project tracking. The role serves as a key resource for participating sites, community health workers (CHWs), providers, implementation partners, and regional leadership, helping ensure regional activities are completed efficiently, consistently, and in alignment with project timelines, reporting requirements, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes.

The Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative is a grant funded, statewide, evidence-based digital therapeutic strategy designed to expand access to treatment for depression, substance use disorders (SUD) and other mental disorders in rural Kansas. The initiative deploys clinically validated computerized mental health interventions supported by community-based facilitation and integrated into rural primary care, behavioral health, and community settings.

We are currently recruiting for three program coordinator positions.

Job Description:

Job Duties

Regional Deployment & Site Coordination

  • Track completion of regional onboarding, deployment, and access setup activities for participating sites. Maintain deployment task lists, implementation documentation, and project records.

  • Schedule and coordinate deployment-related meetings and communications. Log, monitor, and route technical issues to appropriate project personnel and track issue resolution.

  • Maintain records related to deployment activities, onboarding progress, implementation milestones, and site readiness.

  • Support the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring implementation progress, identifying potential barriers, and facilitating successful deployment activities.

Training Coordination & Implementation Support

  • Schedule and coordinate regional training sessions for providers, CHWs, supervisors, navigators, and program staff. Track training attendance, completion, certifications, and related documentation. Distribute training materials, reminders, schedules, and follow-up communications. Serve as the first point of contact for routine implementation questions and assist with resolving common operational concerns.

  • Support onboarding and implementation activities for participating sites, organizations, and staff. Coordinate logistics and facilitate stakeholder communication to support successful adoption of digital mental health services.

Workforce & Program Operations Support

  • Support onboarding logistics for CHWs, case management staff, and other program personnel. Maintain regional staffing rosters, contact lists, distribution lists, and workforce documentation.

  • Coordinate routine communication among CHWs, supervisors, project staff, and participating organizations, and track operational issues and implementation barriers affecting program activities.

  • Document workflow modifications, process updates, and operational improvements to help ensure consistency across participating sites and regional partners.

Evaluation, Reporting & Continuous Quality Improvement

  • Track regional data submission schedules, reporting deadlines, and project deliverables. Coordinate meetings associated with evaluation activities, reporting reviews, and CQI initiatives.

  • Document meeting notes, action items, decisions, and follow-up tasks, and maintain records for grant administration, reporting, and project documentation.

  • Support preparation and dissemination of summaries, reports, presentations, slide decks, and stakeholder communications.

  • Assist the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring completion of CQI action items and reporting requirements.

User Support & Access Coordination

  • Coordinate logistics associated with participant, provider, and stakeholder support activities. Track access-related issues reported by users, CHWs, providers, and participating sites.

  • Route user access concerns to the appropriate technical or program staff and monitor progress toward resolution. Maintain user-facing support materials, frequently asked questions (FAQs), reference guides, and communication resources.

  • Track recurring access barriers and support identification of trends that require escalation to regional leadership or project management teams.

Regional Communication & Stakeholder Support

  • Support communication among participating healthcare organizations, community partners, providers, and project teams within the regional hub.

  • Coordinate meeting logistics, maintain distribution lists, prepare communications, and facilitate follow-up activities related to project implementation.

  • Assist in maintaining positive relationships with participating organizations and stakeholders.

  • Support dissemination of project updates, training opportunities, implementation resources, and program information throughout the region.

Integration with Regional & Statewide Program Operations

  • Support the Regional Hub Program Manager in ensuring alignment between regional implementation activities and statewide project goals.

  • Maintain documentation, records, and communications that support coordination across regional hubs and statewide leadership teams.

  • Participate in statewide coordination meetings, implementation activities, and quality improvement initiatives as assigned.

  • Assist in sharing lessons learned, implementation best practices, and operational insights across project teams and partner organizations.

  • Conducts activities in a professional and ethical manner, and in accordance with KUMC Policies and applicable local, state and federal laws and regulations.

  • Performs job responsibilities in a safe and secure manner.

  • Coordinate work with other University areas ensure integration and support of the University mission.

  • Develops, maintains and expands job-specific knowledge and skills to keep pace with industry changes and supports the university's commitment to excellence and innovation.

  • Participates in relevant committees, task force, or other similar activities.

  • Maintain confidentiality of medical center, employee, and patient information. Manages sensitive data with discretion and in accordance with KUMC policies and legal requirements.

  • Maintains the highest standards of integrity, respect, professional conduct, and ethical standards.

description:

About the Role:

On the Engineering Systems team at CrowdStrike, we operate and maintain many of the systems and services that support the build, test, signing, and deployment of our software to the cloud and to our customers, as well as providing consultation, troubleshooting, and engineering support for the creation and maintenance of the pipelines that provide those functions.   • Experience writing Groovy for Jenkins pipeline development (Jenkinsfiles, shared libraries)

description:

Ready to make a difference in the lives of others? Join our world-class team of genetic counselors!

Learn more about the Center of Genomic Medicine at Cedars-Sinai Guerin Children's:

As a Genetic Counselor II, you will deliver comprehensive genetic counseling services to patients and families in accordance with established professional practice guidelines. Clinical responsibilities are generally centered in an assigned practice area, with flexibility to provide clinical coverage across other practice areas based on departmental and organizational needs.

  • Responsible for analyzing the intake information and determining if appropriate appointments have been scheduled.

  • Provides genetic counseling in accordance w/applicable standards of professional care.
  • Attends continuous education courses, attends meetings, and reviews medical literature. Stays current in GC field.

  • Contributes to quality/development of clinical services, participates in specialty sections, and coordinates specific services or specific projects.

  • Provides comprehensive genetic counseling services for programs in the Center for Genomic Medicine, as assigned, which may include adult and pediatric patients in general and subspecialty clinics.

  • Minimum of two (2) years experience in genetic counseling and competent in all genetic counselor core functions required.

  • Experience in adult genetics and/or pediatric genetics is preferred.

title: Sr. Analyst, Competitive Intelligence
location: PA - Philadelphia, 1701 John F Kennedy Blvd
description:
Comcast brings together the best in media and technology. We drive innovation to create the world's best entertainment and online experiences. As a Fortune 50 leader, we set the pace in a variety of innovative and fascinating businesses and create career opportunities across a wide range of locations and disciplines. We are at the forefront of change and move at an amazing pace, thanks to our remarkable people, who bring cutting-edge products and services to life for millions of customers every day. If you share in our passion for teamwork, our vision to revolutionize industries and our goal to lead the future in media and technology, we want you to fast-forward your career at Comcast.

Job Summary

The Market & Competitive Insights team plays a key role in helping shape Comcast's growth strategy, specifically our longer-term path to competitive differentiation. The foundation of our framework is assessing how consumer preferences, priorities, and behaviors are evolving regarding broadband, mobile, entertainment, and smart home services. In conjunction with that effort, we analyze competitor performance and strategies and tactics for meeting those changing consumer needs. That consumer/competitive/market view provides the context for the longer-term path we help define for Comcast to deliver unique and compelling services that resonate with consumers and differentiate us in the process.

The Sr. Analyst, Competitive Intelligence will play a key role in helping the organization understand and respond to changes across the internet, mobile, and entertainment markets. This role will systematically monitor shifts in competitor strategies, tactics, and performance, while assessing the impact of competitive, consumer, and macroeconomic trends on the business. By translating market developments and competitive performance into actionable insights, the Sr. Analyst will help identify areas of competitive advantage and opportunity nationally and regionally and inform both near-term tactical decisions and longer-term strategic planning.

Job Description

Responsibilities:

  • Monitor and analyze changes in the competitive landscape across internet, mobile, and entertainment, including competitor strategies, product offerings, pricing, promotions, GTM activity, and other key developments.
  • Track and assess competitor and industry performance, including quarterly results, subscriber trends, financial performance, and relevant operating metrics.
  • Identify and quantify the impact of competitive, consumer, and macroeconomic factors on market and business performance.
  • Synthesize complex market and competitive information into clear, actionable insights that highlight key implications for the business.
  • Develop executive ready presentations and compelling storylines that translate complex competitive and market analyses into clear insights, implications, and recommended actions for senior leadership.
  • Support near term tactical decision making and longer term strategic planning through data driven competitive and market analysis.
  • Build and maintain competitive intelligence tools, frameworks, and reporting that enable systematic tracking of market developments and performance over time.
  • Partner with teams across the organization to answer key competitive questions and support high priority strategic initiatives.
  • Consistent exercise of independent judgment and discretion in matters of significance.
  • Regular, consistent and punctual attendance. Must be able to work nights and weekends, variable schedule(s) as necessary.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Preferred Skills:

  • Analytical Skills: Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and translate it into actionable insights, particularly regarding customer experience and market strategies.
  • Research Abilities: Experience or coursework in market research, customer experience analysis, and competitive strategy.
  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly and concisely.
  • Proficiency in Tools: Familiarity with data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Power BI) and research platforms (e.g., surveys, databases).
  • Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and contribute to team discussions and decisions.
  • Curiosity & Initiative: A proactive approach to learning and problem-solving, with a strong curiosity about consumer behavior, customer experience, and market dynamics.

Employees at all levels are expected to:

  • Understand our Operating Principles; make them the guidelines for how you do your job.
  • Own the customer experience think and act in ways that put our customers first, give them seamless digital options at every touchpoint, and make them promoters of our products and services.
  • Know your stuff be enthusiastic learners, users and advocates of our game-changing technology, products and services, especially our digital tools and experiences.
  • Win as a team make big things happen by working together and being open to new ideas.
  • Be an active part of the Net Promoter System a way of working that brings more employee and customer feedback into the company by joining huddles, making call backs and helping us elevate opportunities to do better for our customers.
  • Drive results and growth.
  • Support a culture of inclusion in how you work and lead.
  • Do what's right for each other, our customers, investors and our communities.

title: Gerente de Restaurante
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Areas of responsibility include Restaurants/Bars and Room Service, if applicable. Supervises daily restaurant operations and assists with menu planning, maintains sanitation standards and assists servers and hosts on the floor during peak meal periods. Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction and maximize the financial performance in areas of responsibility. Determines training needed to accomplish goals, then implements plan.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Food Service Management, Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; 2 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, or related professional area.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Day-to-Day Operations

• Supervises and manages employees. Manages all day-to-day operations. Understands employee positions well enough to perform duties in employees' absence.

• Maintains service and sanitation standards in restaurant, bar/lounge and room service areas.

• Reviews staffing levels to ensure that guest service, operational needs and financial objectives are met.

Leading Food and Beverage Team

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making; demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Serves as a role model to demonstrate appropriate behaviors.

• Identifies the developmental needs of others and coaches, mentors, or otherwise helps others to improve their knowledge or skills.

• Develops specific goals and plans to prioritize, organize, and accomplish your work.

• Ensures and maintains the productivity level of employees.

• Provides the leadership, vision and direction to bring together and prioritize the departmental goals in a way that will be efficient and effective.

• Ensures compliance with all food & beverage policies, standards and procedures by training, supervising, follow-up and hands on management.

• Ensures compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

• Ensures compliance with food handling and sanitation standards.

• Ensures staff understands local, state and Federal liquor laws.

• Establishes and maintains open, collaborative relationships with employees and ensures employees do the same within the team.

• Establishes guidelines so employees understand expectations and parameters.

• Monitors alcohol beverage service in compliance with local laws.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Provides services that are above and beyond for customer satisfaction and retention.

• Improves service by communicating and assisting individuals to understand guest needs, providing guidance, feedback, and individual coaching when needed.

• Manages day-to-day operations, ensures the quality, standards and meets the expectations of the customers on a daily basis.

• Displays leadership in guest hospitality, exemplifies excellent customer service and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Empowers employees to provide excellent customer service.

• Acts as the guest service role model for the restaurants, sets a good example of excellent customer service and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Handles guest problems and complaints.

• Meets with guests on an informal basis during meals or upon departure to obtain feedback on quality of food and beverage, service levels and overall satisfaction.

• Ensures corrective action is taken to continuously improve service results.

• Incorporates guest satisfaction as a component of departmental meetings with a focus on continuous improvement.

• Manages service delivery in outlets to ensure excellent service from point of entry to departure (e.g., greeting from hostess, speed of order taking and food and beverage delivery, fulfillment of special requests, collection of payment & invitation to return).

Managing and Conducting Human Resource Activities

• Provides guidance and direction to subordinates, including setting performance standards and monitoring performance.

• Identifies the educational needs of others, develops formal educational or training programs or classes, and teaches or instructs others.

• Ensures employees are treated fairly and equitably. Strives to improve employee retention.

• Ensures employees receive on-going training to understand guest expectations.

• Solicits employee feedback, utilizes an "open door" policy and reviews employee satisfaction results to identify and address employee problems or concerns.

• Strives to improve service performance.

• Ensures recognition is taking place across areas of responsibility.

Additional Responsibilities

• Provides information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

• Analyzes information and evaluating results to choose the best solution and solve problems.

• Assists servers and hosts on the floor during meal periods and high demand times.

• Recognizes good quality products and presentations.

• Supervises daily shift operations in absence of Assistant Restaurant Manager.

• Oversees the financial aspects of the department including purchasing and payment of invoices.

title: Backstage Captain, Garden State Plaza - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As a Selling and Support Captain, you are an advocate for the customer and a role model for your colleagues. As an elevated hourly colleague, you are an expert in customer satisfaction , merchandising, and building brand loyalty. You will drive results through promotional and Omni selling initiatives. Under the supervision of a People Leader, you will play a key role in communicating expectations and priorities to our colleagues. Advancement opportunities include Personal Stylist or Sales and Customer Experience Manager.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice
  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

What You Will Do

  • Based upon your Captain assignment you could be fulfilling customer orders, merchandising, processing new products, or supervising the selling floor in delivering exceptional customer service.
  • Lead colleagues in the execution and completion of assigned tasks.
  • As an advocate for the customer, you will role model and provide fast feedback on how to make every customer experience outstanding.
  • Ensure high-level of customer service through problem-solving and customer-focused resolutions.
  • Enhance the in-store customer experience by promoting our Macy's mobile app.
  • Meet with People Leaders throughout the day to plan and monitor total store activities.
  • Provide People Leaders continuous feedback that drives a positive customer experience and improves our processes.
  • Perform store opening and closing procedures, including accessing alarm system and settling the registers.
  • Lead and participate in the adherence to our best in class merchandise standards.
  • Educate colleagues on point of sale technology, radio frequency equipment, and applications to assist in selling and fulfillment of customer orders.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships, and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Who You Are

  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Proficient in communicating effectively with customers and providing clear direction to colleagues
  • Self-starter in adapting quickly to changing customer expectations and needs
  • Resourceful and able to adapt quickly to changing priorities and deadlines
  • 1-2 years of direct retail experience preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Involves standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 50lbs., stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders.
  • Reaching, including above eye level, crouching, kneeling, stooping and color vision.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Asset Protection Detective, Westland - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story.

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Detective, you will help protect company assets, reduce shortage, and support a safe, customer-focused shopping environment. Using surveillance, investigative tools, and strong partnerships with store teams and law enforcement, you will identify and respond to theft, recover merchandise, and help protect our customers, colleagues, and business.

Why This Role Matters

Asset Protection Detectives play an important role in reducing loss while maintaining a safe and welcoming store environment. Through training, observation, investigation, and de-escalation, this role helps protect company assets, support colleagues, and ensure customers can shop with confidence.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

What To Expect

  • Use surveillance techniques, investigative tools, and reporting systems to help identify theft, dishonest activity, and shortage trends.
  • Partner with Asset Protection leaders, store teams, and law enforcement to support investigations and protect company assets.
  • Apply de-escalation tools and sound judgment to help maintain a safe environment for customers and colleagues.
  • Prepare clear documentation, statements, and evidence to support investigations, audits, and legal proceedings.
  • Support team readiness by training colleagues on protocols that help protect company assets.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Help protect customers, colleagues, and company assets by identifying, investigating, and responding to theft and dishonest activity.
  • Use surveillance techniques to support the apprehension of shoplifters and dishonest employees, while following company policies and legal requirements.
  • Recover stolen merchandise and provide statements, evidence, and documentation to support investigations.
  • Prepare timely and accurate reports related to theft incidents, investigations, audits, and assigned activities.
  • Build strong partnerships with store colleagues, Asset Protection leaders, and law enforcement to support investigations and shortage reduction.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, and evidence preservation.
  • Testify in court for criminal and civil cases, as needed.
  • Respond to alarm calls, support special assignments, and facilitate first aid for customers and colleagues when needed.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Ability to observe, identify, and respond to suspicious activity in a retail environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with customers, colleagues, leaders, and law enforcement.

  • Ability to use sound judgment, de-escalation tools, and company procedures to support a safe environment.

  • Ability to handle proprietary, sensitive, and confidential information with discretion and integrity.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail, customer service, asset protection, security, investigations, or law enforcement.

  • Ability to prepare accurate reports, statements, and documentation related to incidents and investigations.

  • Experience using surveillance systems, reporting tools, or investigative technology.

  • Ability to train or coach colleagues on asset protection protocols, shortage reduction, or safety practices.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.
  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department.
  • May occasionally involve reaching above eye level, stooping, kneeling, or crouching.
  • Must be able to apprehend shoplifters.
  • Ability to sustain long periods of time enclosed in surveillance areas.
  • Frequently lift/move up to 30lbs.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

title: Senior Well Engineer
description:
Mission

The Senior Well Engineer located in St.Johns Newfoundland is responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering support for drilling and well construction activities on complex offshore projects. The role requires strong well engineering expertise, operational knowledge, and the ability to identify, evaluate, and implement technologies and practices that improve drilling performance, safety, efficiency, and well delivery outcomes.

The Senior Well Engineer serves as a key technical resource supporting well planning, operational performance analysis, technology deployment, continuous improvement initiatives, and collaboration between multidisciplinary teams throughout the well construction lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Well Engineering & Planning

  • Support well design, planning, and execution activities for drilling and well construction operations.
  • Participate in risk assessments, technical reviews, and operational readiness activities.
  • Ensure application of engineering standards, best practices, and lessons learned throughout project execution.

Drilling Performance & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze drilling performance data to identify trends, recurring challenges, and improvement opportunities.
  • Lead or participate in flat-time reduction and drilling efficiency initiatives.
  • Monitor well delivery performance against technical and operational objectives.
  • Support benchmarking and performance reviews across wells, rigs, and campaigns.
  • Develop recommendations to improve operational efficiency and well construction performance.
  • Identify opportunities to improve drilling efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance operational performance.

Technology Evaluation & Implementation

  • Identify and evaluate emerging drilling, completions, and well construction technologies.
  • Develop technical recommendations in supporting technology adoption.
  • Collaborate with technical specialists, service providers, and operational teams to transition technologies from concept to field deployment.

Engineering Studies & Problem Solving

  • Lead engineering studies to resolve drilling and well construction challenges.
  • Conduct root cause investigations and develop corrective action recommendations.
  • Support analysis of wellbore stability, lost circulation, drilling dysfunctions, equipment performance, cementing challenges, and other operational issues.
  • Capture and communicate lessons learned to support continuous improvement.

  • Degree in Engineering.
  • 5+ years’ experience in drilling and well construction engineering.
  • Offshore drilling experience
  • Strong understanding of well design, drilling operations, well delivery processes, and performance optimization.
  • Demonstrated experience evaluating and implementing new technologies.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with operators, drilling contractors, and service providers.
  • Proven ability to identify opportunities, drive technical improvements, and deliver operational value.

title: Counsel
description:
The American Psychological Association (APA), a large non-profit organization seeks a practical, collaborative lawyer with 3-5 years’ experience to serve as in-house Counsel providing day-to-day legal support for division and program legal support, general and federal contract review, “start-up”-related business legal support, public and private fundraising/development, conflicts of interest, and litigation support. Experience in election law, lobbying rules, and tax-exemption compliance a plus. This role works closely with the General Counsel, Deputy General Counsel, and Associate General Counsel and Office of General Counsel paralegals and administrative staff. This lawyer also works closely with APA staff at most levels of the organization, APA elected and appointed leaders, Divisions, APA governance bodies, outside counsel, and external parties to provide timely, strategic, and accurate in-house corporate counsel and risk management advice.

Salary range ($107,000-$149,000)

Note: The APA operates on a 37.5-hour work week with one-hour lunch breaks each day. APA’s salaries are based on several considerations, including years of relevant experience, budgetary parameters, level of education, and previous staff and/or governance experience at APA.

Education And Experience Required

  • J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school. Active member in good standing of the District of Columbia Bar, or a bar eligible for waiver into D.C. Three to five years of progressive legal experience in one or more of the preferred practice areas: non-profit, association, governance, contracts lifecycle management, and grants (including governmental—federal and other public entities--and private), corporate compliance, and litigation support. Familiarity with election law, tax-exempt organization law, and general legal counseling preferred.
  • Strong generalist instincts, sound judgment, and the ability to spot and address legal issues involving multiple subjects under deadline. Comfortable learning new areas of law quickly as business needs arise.
  • Exceptional analytic and critical thinking skills. Strong interpersonal, negotiating, and collaborative skills. Clear, concise communicator, both written and verbal, with the ability to translate complex legal concepts into practical guidance to organizational stakeholders, executive leadership, Board members, governance bodies, and volunteer leaders.
  • Thrive in a small, fast-paced general counsel’s office. Experience working with staff and volunteers on legal guidance, project planning, compliance, risk assessment, operational approvals, and issue escalation.

Computer Skills Required

General fluency with Microsoft Office, remote meeting programs such as Teams and Zoom, contract management systems, project management tools, APA-approved AI tools, and other business, workflow, and collaboration software. Technical ability to adapt quickly to new systems and to use technology to organize intake, track matters, summarize issues, prioritize projects, and manage legal workflows.

Responsibilities

  • Serves as a day-to-day legal resource for APA divisions and business units, providing guidance, compliance support, first-line review, and risk management strategies on operational matters. Triages incoming legal questions to the appropriate OGC workflow and helps internal clients understand compliance requirements, decision points, and when to escalate.
  • Manages the contract lifecycle for assigned APA matters, including review, drafting, and occasionally negotiation. Contract types include program agreements, vendor and consulting engagements, service agreements, event contracts, NDAs, data agreements, and other operational agreements.
  • Partners with assigned APA revenue-generating team(s) to identify legal and business risks, recommend revisions, drive timely contract review. Provides ongoing program counsel and operational approval. Collaborates with OGC colleagues on governance “internal law” compliance and risk management, including conflicts of interest.
  • Provides legal support for government contracts, government grants, and private grants, including review of funding agreements, grant terms, compliance obligations, flow-down requirements, reporting obligations, certifications, and operational risks. Works with APA staff to flag legal issues in APA staff grant and contract administration and to support compliance.
  • Provides litigation support, including internal fact development, document collection coordination, discovery support, initial review and potential management of incoming third-party and regular subpoenas, preservation and information-gathering support, and liaison work with outside counsel. Coordinates with OGC colleagues, APA staff, and outside counsel to support handling appropriate internal communication.
  • Serves as first point of contact within OGC for APA staff, Divisions, programs, elected and appointed leaders, and governance participants on division legal matters.
  • Experience preferred for candidates with familiarity with federal exempt-organization law for Section 501(c)(3) and Section 501(c)(6) organizations and political action committees applicable to APA compliance obligations.
  • Collaborates across APA—staff, governance bodies and leaders, and outside professional organizations-- on projects within assigned practice areas. Represents OGC on internal APA committees and work groups. Coordinates with outside counsel on assigned matters, including litigation, subpoenas, grants, and contracts. Supports fellow OGC lawyers on special projects and cross-functional legal priorities as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

About APA:

The American Psychological Association (APA) represents 146,000 psychologists, students, and affiliates, primarily in the U.S. and Canada but also in other countries around the world. APA is a scientific and professional organization with about 500 employees and is categorized as a 501(c)(3) along with its 501(c)(6) companion organization, APA Services, Inc.

APA offers a generous employee benefits program, including Remote Work/Flexible Scheduling; a 401(k) option with employer match of up to 4%; medical, dental, and vision insurance options and an outpatient mental health benefit; paid personal/vacation time plus 12 paid holidays; Family/Medical Leave; tuition assistance; an Employee Assistance Program (EAP); short- and long-term disability insurance; and more.

Job Location: Remote: APA jobs may be considered for remote work eligibility as defined in APA’s Flexible Work Policy and are subject to approval. Remote work employees may not work from the following states or U.S. territories: Alaska, California, Colorado, Guam, Hawaii, Iowa, Louisiana, Montana, Nebraska, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, U.S. Virgin Islands, Washington, Wyoming.

Application Instructions:

Qualified candidates must apply online through APA’s applicant system and attach a resume and cover letter specifying your salary expectations. Applications that are submitted without both documents are considered incomplete and will not be reviewed for consideration. Once your application is submitted, you will receive a confirmation email.Please make sure to check your Spam folder if you do not receive an email from us.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, personal appearance, familial status, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. #LIRemote#LIRemote

title: Laboratory Assistant, Clinical Laboratory (Per Diem, Evening Shift)
description:
Central to all that California has to offer, Adventist Health Bakersfield has been providing an extraordinary team of world-class physicians, top-notch medical technology, caring professionals and award-winning quality since 1910. We are comprised of a 254-bed acute care hospital and 20 primary and specialty care medical offices. As one of America's fastest growing cities, Bakersfield offers affordable housing on the West Coast, beautiful weather, high-quality education and it is just a few hours away from Yosemite and Sequoia National Parks, the Central California Coast and Southern California's great sports, theaters, concerts and amusement parks.

Job Summary:

Collects blood specimens, as well as receives, handles and processes specimens for Laboratory testing. Receives, sorts and accessions specimens, assigning to appropriate pre-analytic and analytic workflow. Completes computerized tasks related to patient registration and/or test order entry, specimen collection, receiving and processing. Performs basic post-analytic tasks, including distributing reports, storing and/or retrieving specimens. Completes quality-related tasks such as documentation of work, maintaining a clean, stocked and safe work area, and monitoring pending work, as well as escalating priority work. Operates and/or uses basic pre-analytic lab equipment. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI
  • Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
  • Experience in Phlebotomy in acute care environment: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (CPTI) license: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI

Facility Specific License/Certifications:

  • Phlebotomy Tech (CPT) or Certified Phlebotomy Technician II (CPTII): Required

Essential Functions:

  • Collects blood specimens for a variety of Laboratory tests using age-appropriate techniques; handles/transports Lab specimens and provides post-phlebotomy care to patients. Receives specimens for testing; assesses specimens upon receipt according to established criteria to determine acceptability and takes action according to protocol including escalating to licensed or certified personnel for direction. Handles and processes a variety of specimen types to prepare them for analysis; adheres to protocols to maintain specimen integrity at all times.
  • Completes computerized tasks as appropriate for affiliate to ensure complete patient registration and/or test order entry into the lab information system, as well as generation of collection lists and/or labels. Prepares and/or packages specimens for transport to another Adventist Health or outside reference laboratory and may complete computer steps necessary for processing referred specimens.
  • Maintains an adequate inventory of supplies in work area and/or on phlebotomy cart. Maintains required records by completing basic documentation of pre-analytic and post-analytic work, as well as quality-related tasks. Participates in managing the laboratory workflow by performing duties such as monitoring pending work, escalating priority work, locating specimens, and coordinating specimen recollections.
  • Verbally communicates released/reported results. Routes, distributes and retransmits released/reported results. Stores and retrieves specimens.
  • Receives incoming calls for the laboratory and assists the caller as appropriate or transfers these calls to the appropriate laboratory section or person. Communicates with customer to clarify ambiguous, unclear or duplicate test orders.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Organizational Requirements:

Adventist Health is committed to the safety and wellbeing of our associates and patients. Therefore, we require that all associates receive all required vaccinations as a condition of employment and annually thereafter, where applicable. Medical and religious exemptions may apply.

Adventist Health participates in E-Verify. Visit https://adventisthealth.org/careers/everify/ for more information about E-Verify. By choosing to apply, you acknowledge that you have accessed and read the E-Verify Participation and Right to Work notices and understand the contents therein.

description:

Job Category: Engineering and Technical Support

The Opportunity:

CACI is seeking a Quality Assurance Manager to support our U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DS) customer. This position leads enterprise quality assurance efforts supporting Agile software development, DevSecOps, and IT service delivery across a dynamic federal IT environment.

The successful candidate will collaborate with Development, Security, Operations, Project Managers, and Product Owners to establish software quality standards, oversee testing strategies, implement quality metrics, and drive continuous improvement throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). This role is instrumental in ensuring software solutions are secure, maintainable, testable, and compliant with applicable federal and organizational standards.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead quality assurance activities across Agile software development projects.

  • Establish and maintain quality standards throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC).

  • Ensure compliance with applicable federal and organizational standards, including NIST, OWASP, and Section 508.

  • Review project deliverables and conduct quality reviews at key lifecycle milestones.

  • Develop QA strategies supporting automated and manual testing.

  • Oversee test planning, test case development, Independent Verification & Validation (IV&V), and User Acceptance Testing (UAT).

  • Partner with Agile teams to integrate quality practices into sprint planning, releases, and DevSecOps pipelines.

  • Define and monitor automated quality gates using tools such as SonarQube, Fortify, CAST, or similar platforms.

  • Develop dashboards and report quality metrics, including defect trends, test coverage, code quality, security findings, and release readiness.

  • Present quality metrics and recommendations to program leadership and Government stakeholders.

  • Maintain QA policies, standards, and supporting documentation.

  • Deliver training on quality assurance processes, testing methodologies, and quality tools.

  • Drive continuous process improvement through lessons learned, retrospectives, and Agile quality best practices.


Qualifications:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field.

  • 7+ years of experience leading software quality assurance in Agile development environments.

  • Experience with Agile methodologies, Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), DevSecOps, and software testing practices.

  • Experience implementing automated testing and software quality tools such as SonarQube, Fortify, CAST, Azure DevOps, Jira, or similar platforms.

  • Knowledge of secure software development principles and federal standards, including NIST and OWASP.

  • Experience developing quality metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting.

  • Strong communication, collaboration, and organizational skills.

  • Active Secret Clearance or the ability to obtain and maintain one.


Desired:

  • Agile certification (CSM, PMI-ACP, SAFe, or equivalent).

  • PMP, CSQE, ISTQB, or similar professional certification.

  • Experience supporting Department of State or other federal civilian IT programs.

  • Experience implementing DevSecOps or CI/CD quality practices in enterprise environments.

-

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

The AI/ML Engineer – School (K-12) delivers AI solutions tailored to K-12 educators, students, and administrators. You will build production AI features that save teachers time on lesson planning and grading, provide personalized support to students, and do so under the strictest compliance and safety standards of any education segment.

This role is unique because K-12 demands more than technical skill — it demands sensitivity to child safety, FERPA compliance, COPPA considerations, and the realities of how teachers actually work. The ideal candidate has shipped K-12 or consumer-safe AI features before and understands that in this domain, 'safe by default' is table stakes.

Key Responsibilities

K-12 AI Feature Development

  • Build AI tools for teacher lesson planning, worksheet creation, and content adaptation

  • Develop AI-powered grading, feedback, and formative assessment features

  • Create age-appropriate student support, tutoring, and help experiences

  • Build administrator analytics and early-warning systems for student intervention

  • Integrate AI capabilities into the Cengage School product ecosystem

Compliance & Child Safety

  • Ensure FERPA, COPPA, and state-level student data privacy compliance in every feature

  • Implement child safety guardrails, content filtering, and age-appropriate AI behavior

  • Partner with Governance on policy enforcement for minors and classroom contexts

  • Handle parent, district, and state-level data privacy and audit requirements

  • Build transparency and explainability into AI features used with minors

Optimization & Impact

  • Optimize features based on teacher usage data and feedback

  • Measure teacher adoption rates, time saved per educator, and classroom impact

  • Partner with curriculum and learning science teams on efficacy measurement

  • Iterate rapidly while maintaining compliance posture at every release

  • Maintain documentation and engineering runbooks for all deployed features

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field

  • 4+ years of experience in software engineering, with at least 2 years focused on AI/ML

  • Strong proficiency in Python with experience building production ML or LLM systems

  • Hands-on experience with modern AI APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock)

  • Strong understanding of FERPA, COPPA, and education data privacy requirements

  • Experience building AI systems with safety, content filtering, and guardrails

  • Solid software engineering fundamentals including testing, CI/CD, and system design

  • Excellent judgment on child safety and age-appropriate design decisions

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience building AI features for K-12 or consumer-safe environments

  • Background in EdTech with direct teacher or classroom exposure

  • Familiarity with state-level student data privacy regulations (SOPIPA, New York Ed Law 2-d)

  • Experience with content moderation, red-teaming, or AI safety evaluation

  • Familiarity with agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex)

  • Experience with accessibility standards (WCAG, Section 508, DOJ accessibility)

Tools & Technologies

You should be comfortable with many of the following:

  • Languages: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, SQL

  • AI/ML: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, LangChain, Hugging Face

  • Safety: Content moderation APIs, custom guardrail systems, red-team frameworks

  • Cloud: AWS (Lambda, ECS, SageMaker, Bedrock), Azure OpenAI

  • Data: Snowflake, Databricks, Postgres, Redis

  • DevOps: Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, CI/CD pipelines

Key Competencies

  • Child Safety First — makes conservative design choices when minors are involved

  • Compliance Rigor — builds FERPA/COPPA compliance into every feature from the start

  • Teacher Empathy — understands the realities of classroom workflow and time pressure

  • Shipping Mindset — delivers features on cadence while maintaining compliance posture

  • Technical Craft — writes clean, tested, production-grade code

  • Collaboration — partners effectively with product, legal, and curriculum teams

What We Offer

  • Opportunity to shape AI at scale across a global learning company

  • Direct impact on business outcomes, product, and workforce productivity

  • Access to cutting-edge AI tools, platforms, and technologies

  • Collaborative team environment focused on innovation and continuous improvement

LOB Description:

  • High visibility role with direct interaction with senior technology and business leaders.
  • Opportunity to make a measurable impact on the firm's operational resilience and regulatory readiness.
  • Exposure to enterprise-scale technologies and recovery solutions.
  • Ability to influence resiliency outcomes across a large and diverse application portfolio.
  • Strong opportunities to develop expertise in business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
  • Involvement in strategic initiatives focused on strengthening the firm's ability to respond to and recover from disruptive events.

LOB Responsibilities:

  • Lead and coordinate annual resiliency testing activities to strengthen application recoverability, operational resilience, and compliance with Bank standards.
  • Partner with Application Managers and Production Support teams to ensure applications are prepared for testing and recovery strategies are validated through successful test execution.
  • Track application testing readiness and performance, ensuring recovery capabilities align with Bank of America resiliency standards, Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs), and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
  • Monitor testing compliance metrics and drive remediation efforts for applications that are non-compliant, overdue, or unable to meet established recovery requirements.
  • Provide analysis, status reporting, and risk commentary for late, failed, or at-risk testing activities, including escalation of issues requiring management attention.
  • Facilitate post-test reviews and corrective action planning to address identified gaps and improve overall resiliency and recoverability.
  • Partner with technology and business stakeholders to prioritize testing activities, resolve obstacles, and ensure deliverables are completed within required timeframes.
  • Communicate, influence, and negotiate effectively across all organizational levels to identify resources, drive accountability, and achieve program objectives.

Job Description:
Individual provides technical consulting and coordination of corporate vendor information security and business continuity testing services to internal clients. Demonstrates a high level of technical proficiency necessary to recommend and implement required solutions and/or execute processes that protect the bank's assets. Participates or leads technical business continuity and vendor initiatives to support ongoing process activities (information security/business continuity vendor assessments, mainframe and/or midrange application and technical infrastructure recovery testing, internal and external vendor testing, event management and progress reporting/measurement). May provide technology based business continuity, information security or vendor subject matter consulting support in audit and regulatory matters as needed. Must be able to work under close or minimal supervision with guidance from manager or team lead as necessary.

Required Qualifications:

  • Strong knowledge of Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, Operational Resiliency Testing, and Compliance Risk Management processes.
  • Advanced proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel (including automation, reporting, and data analysis capabilities), PowerPoint, SharePoint, Access, and Visio, with the ability to create executive-ready reports, dashboards, and presentations.
  • Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new systems, technologies, and processes while delivering results in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proven ability to independently lead complex projects from planning through execution with minimal management oversight.
  • Strong experience coordinating with multiple stakeholders across business, technology, infrastructure, and support teams to successfully plan and execute Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery exercises.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes and drive accountability across diverse stakeholder groups. Experience tracking compliance metrics, managing remediation efforts, and providing risk-based reporting and status updates to leadership.
  • Ability to analyze complex issues, identify root causes, and develop practical solutions to improve resiliency, recoverability, and operational effectiveness.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines in a highly regulated environment.
  • Experience supporting audit, regulatory, and governance activities related to Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, or Operational Resiliency programs.

Desired Qualifications:

  • JIRA Experience
  • Continuity Planning Tool Experience
  • Prior experience with Business Continuity processes and tools is desirable
  • Preferred process improvement and Operational Excellence exposure
  • Creativity – able to look at a problem from a new perspective and to develop new ideas and solutions
  • Ability to understand new technologies, intellectually curious.

description:

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Help Build the Future of Caterpillar – Be Part of What’s Next in Autonomous Construction Sites

At Caterpillar, technology always has a purpose, which is to solve our customers’ toughest challenges. Construction autonomy is one of the most complex challenges in applied AI, and at Caterpillar, advancements in physical AI, simulation, sensing, and edge computing are turning things that once felt impossible—intelligent machines operating in dynamic jobsites—into reality.

We are looking for a hands-on QA Lead who can establish quality strategy, validation practices, automation, and release confidence for a foundational simulation platform. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys moving fast, learning new technologies, collaborating across robotics and platform teams, and building a quality culture from the ground up.

What you will do:

  • Lead QA strategy, planning, and execution for the simulation and rendering platform across frontend, backend, data, APIs, rendering, and integration layers.
  • Define quality standards, test processes, release gates, defect triage methods, acceptance criteria, and measurable quality signals for the engineering team.
  • Build and mentor a high-performing QA function, including hiring support, technical interviewing, onboarding, and coaching QA engineers and SDETs.
  • Own automated test architecture for UI, API, integration, regression, data validation, simulation scenarios, rendering validation, and performance/reliability testing.
  • Partner with software engineering, robotics, product, and architecture stakeholders to translate business and technical requirements into testable acceptance criteria and validation plans.
  • Champion CI/CD quality practices, including test selection, pipeline health, flaky-test reduction, code review expectations for testability, and release readiness reporting.
  • Lead exploratory testing, risk reviews, failure-mode analysis, and defect-prevention practices for simulation workflows and robotic use cases.
  • Collaborate tightly with robotics and platform teams to reduce gaps between customer needs, technical implementation, simulation behavior, and delivered quality.
  • Facilitate QA brainstorming, test design reviews, post-release learning, and continuous improvement sessions.
  • Bring a practical, flexible mindset: if there is a better way to improve quality, propose it and help make it real.

Required

  • Experience leading QA or SDET efforts for complex web, platform, simulation, rendering, robotics, mapping, or data-intensive software products.
  • Proven ability to define QA/QC processes, engineering quality standards, release criteria, and team operating practices.
  • Hands-on experience with test automation for modern web applications, APIs, backend services, databases, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Working knowledge of frontend and backend quality concerns, including JavaScript/TypeScript applications, service APIs, data contracts, and cross-browser/device behavior.
  • Experience validating 3D, graphics, geospatial, or simulation-related workflows, including visual correctness, scenario behavior, spatial data, or rendering output.
  • Experience with automation and quality tooling such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Jest, pytest, Postman/Newman, REST/GraphQL testing, ESLint, Webpack, or similar tools.
  • Experience with cloud-based environments such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Firebase, or similar deployment platforms.
  • Ability to use AI-assisted development and testing tools responsibly to accelerate test creation, troubleshooting, analysis, and documentation.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate ambiguity into clear quality risks, plans, and decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies independently and help teams adopt better practices.

Top Candidate:

  • 7+ years of experience in software quality, test automation, SDET, or related engineering roles for complex software platforms.
  • 3+ years leading QA strategy, QA engineers, SDETs, or cross-functional quality initiatives.
  • 5+ years building automated tests for frontend, backend, API, integration, or system-level workflows.
  • 5+ years working in agile software delivery environments with strong collaboration across engineering, product, and stakeholders.
  • Strong scripting or programming skills, preferably in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Node.js.
  • Experience with rendering, simulation platforms, robotics test environments, Nvidia Omniverse, game engines, GIS/terrain mapping, or digital twin technologies is highly desirable.
  • Experience improving CI/CD pipeline quality, release readiness, defect analytics, and long-term maintainability of test suites.
  • Comfortable balancing hands-on execution with technical leadership, mentoring, and process definition.

title: Service Operations Specialist – Active Security Clearance Required
description:
We have an opening for a Service Operations Specialist to support the planning, coordination, and execution of readiness activities for Superblock Operations Management and other high-hazard projects. In this role, you will administer capabilities implementation processes, coordinate multidisciplinary activities, track deliverables, and prepare reports and documentation supporting Management Reviews, Contractor Assessments, and Federal Assessments. You will work with operations, facilities, ES&H, conduct of operations, engineering, project management, and other stakeholders to coordinate readiness activities and resolve complex issues. This position is in the Strategic Deterrence (SD) Directorate.

This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work.

You will

  • Coordinate startup and restart readiness activities in accordance with DOE O 425.1 and applicable Laboratory requirements.
  • Develop and maintain readiness schedules, action-item trackers, milestone plans, and status reports.
  • Coordinate planning meetings, readiness reviews, kickoff meetings, dry runs, interviews, and follow-up activities.
  • Compile and organize Plans of Action, Readiness Review Board materials, lines of inquiry, criteria, schedules, and supporting documentation.
  • Collect, validate, track, and organize objective evidence, including procedures, training records, test results, hazard analyses, maintenance records, and configuration documentation.
  • Work with project schedulers and facility personnel to identify task dependencies, resource needs, schedule risks, and readiness milestones.
  • Coordinate the availability, onboarding, and orientation of readiness review team members.
  • Support assessment teams by coordinating access to documentation, scheduling interviews, tracking requests, and monitoring daily activities.
  • Observe dry runs and operational demonstrations, document observations, and communicate opportunities for improvement.
  • Track corrective actions associated with pre-start and post-start findings, including due dates, closure documentation, and verification status.
  • Prepare summaries, dashboards, and management reports identifying readiness status, risks, trends, and recommended actions.
  • Review procedures and program documents for completeness, consistency, and alignment with applicable requirements.
  • Coordinate implementation activities associated with updates to Documented Safety Analyses, Technical Safety Requirements, and related safety-basis documents.
  • Support readiness planning for upcoming systems and activities, including plutonium interface evaluations, AVLIS, and other startup or restart initiatives.
  • Capture lessons learned and recommend process improvements to strengthen future readiness activities.
  • Provide guidance, coordination, and informal mentoring to personnel participating in readiness preparation and assessment activities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire.
  • Associate degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Experience coordinating policies and procedure documentation.
  • Ability to analyze data, prepare reports, and support recurring administrative and operational functions.
  • Ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders and manage several tasks at once.
  • Experience with Documented Safety Analyses, Technical Safety Requirements, safety-basis documentation, or comparable high-hazard programs.
  • Experience developing schedules, tracking deliverables and corrective actions, maintaining records and reports, and analyzing operational or planning information.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, resolve process issues, meet deadlines, and coordinate multidisciplinary activities across organizational boundaries.
  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to summarize complex information and present recommendations to management.

Qualifications We Desire

  • Experience supporting DOE O 425.1 startup or restart activities, including LMRs, CRAs, ORRs, or FRAs, at LLNL, a DOE/NNSA national laboratory, or a comparable high-hazard federal facility.
  • Familiarity with Laboratory policies, procedures, regulations, and standards applicable to Superblock operations and Strategic Deterrence.
  • Experience working with outside Regulatory Agencies.
  • Experience using project management, scheduling, database, dashboard, or document-management tools to track readiness activities and report results.
  • Experience developing performance measures, analyzing trends, recommending process improvements, and providing training, coordination, or mentoring to less-experienced personnel.

Pay Range

$113,400 - $138,888 annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. title: Research Associate I - Svendsen Lab - Regenerative Medicine Institute
description:
Job Description

Join Dr. Clive Svendsen and his research group as a Research Associate I in the Cedars-Sinai Regenerative Medicine Institute!

The Svendsen Laboratory at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, Regenerative Medicine Institute is looking for personnel to join our dynamic group. The mission of the Svendsen Laboratory is to study neurodegenerative diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), Huntington’s disease (HD), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS) using stem cells as a disease treatment, as well as a tool for modeling these diseases in vitro. Clive Svendsen, PhD, has significant experience in studying these diseases over the last twenty years and is merging his experience with the use of leading-edge technologies, such as inducible pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells). To learn more, please visit: Svendsen Research Lab | Cedars-Sinai (cedars-sinai.edu).

Are you ready to be a part of breakthrough research?

The incumbent should have an interest in the basic science of stem cells and neuroscience. By understanding how the cells grow and differentiate we will be able to produce a better cell for transplantation and develop techniques for disease modeling.

Working under direct supervision, the Research Associate I performs a variety of routine experimental protocols and procedures to support the objectives of one or more laboratory research projects in a specific area of research. Assists in general laboratory activities, including maintenance of reagents and stocking of supplies. Files and monitors documents. Keeps accurate and detailed records of experiments and results. Assists in the operation of specialized equipment and machinery. Observes safety standards and procedures. The Research Assistant I will be able to perform routine cellular, micro- and molecular biology procedures including, but not limited to Western, Northern blot, DNA/RNA, PCR, protein extraction, cell culture, Immunohistochemistry, and staining. This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.

Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Performs a variety of routine laboratory tasks and procedures.
  • Keeps accurate and detailed project records of experiments and results.
  • May assist with animal husbandry.
  • Maintains lab equipment and related records.
  • Transports, processes and logs samples.
  • Maintains computer database with relevant clinical information.
  • Performs lab maintenance duties, including glassware cleaning and sterilization.
  • Maintains stocks of general lab materials, and places orders for lab equipment and supplies.
  • Assists new students and fellows at the laboratory.
  • Assists in the operation of specialized equipment and machinery.
  • Observes and complies with safety standards and procedures.

Qualifications

Education:

  • Minimum of a Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree in biological science required.

Experience and Skills:

  • Understanding of general research objectives.
  • Working knowledge of database management, personal computers, and presentation and imaging software.
  • Familiar with routine laboratory procedures and experimental protocols.
  • Must possess computer skills to include, but not limited to, Excel and Word.
  • Scheduling flexibility and timeliness including evening, weekend, and holiday rotation commitment. Travel may be required.

description:

Your work will span validation across both cloud-side backend services and UI applications, ensuring the system behaves correctly at every stage — from individual components to full system behavior. This is an opportunity to work at unprecedented scale with cutting-edge cloud technologies while making a direct impact on organizations worldwide, protecting them from sophisticated AI-based threats.

  • Mentor team members on testing methodologies, secure coding practices, and quality engineering

  • Leverage new open source solutions and AI-powered tools to build innovative testing approaches

What You'll Need:

  • 3+ years building testing frameworks and tooling for a Cloud SaaS product or similar SOA

  • Experience contributing to or defining testing strategy at a team or organizational level

  • Experience with cloud services such as AWS, GCP, or OCI, particularly compute and storage offerings

  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency, and drive business outcomes

  • Strong cross-group collaboration and interpersonal communication skills working across engineering organizations

  • Experience mentoring engineers and driving quality culture across a team or organization

Bonus Points:

  • Deep understanding of AI/ML security challenges, threats, and mitigation strategies

  • Experience building, operating, validating, and scaling low-latency cloud services using gRPC and event-driven messaging systems such as Kafka or Pulsar
